body:
## Summary

The Tasks panel header clock (`#tasks-clock`, updated every second by `_tickClock`) is the dominant idle memory producer when the Tasks panel is open: ~1.7 MB/s of renderer growth, confirmed by closing the Tasks panel (the climb stops and memory settles).

## Mechanism

The Tasks modal is draggable, so it is promoted to its own compositor layer. The clock shares that layer, so its 1/sec `textContent` repaint re-rasters the whole modal backing texture (~600×848) every second instead of just the clock (~578×26). On Qt WebEngine those tiles are never evicted (no OS memory-pressure signal), so they accumulate. Measured via `tooling/mem-probe.py` (the only periodic DOM mutation is `#tasks-clock`).

## Fix

Isolate the clock onto its own small compositor layer and contain its paint (`transform: translateZ(0)` + `contain: layout paint` on `.tasks-clock`), so each tick re-rasters ~578×26 instead of ~600×848 (~30× less). Non-visual; keeps the live seconds. Verify with `mem-probe.py slope` with Tasks open, before/after. If insufficient, fall back to minute-resolution updates (60×).
title: Tasks-panel clock re-rasters the whole modal layer every second (~1.7 MB/s); isolate it to its own layer

body:
## Summary

After minimizing and restoring (or refocusing) the window, the web UI becomes unresponsive — tabs/controls cannot be manipulated until the panel is closed and reopened. Cause: the wrapper freezes the page on minimize via `QWebEnginePage.setLifecycleState(LifecycleState.Frozen)` and thaws it on restore with `Active`. Qt documents that this can lose input, and PyQt's lifecycle transitions are unreliable.

## Evidence (Qt docs + PyQt)

- Qt: **"A visible page must remain in the Active state."** (QWebEnginePage)
- Qt: setting a **lower** lifecycle state "may cause side-effects such as ... loss of HTML form input."
- Documented quirk: a refocused frozen page can show blank/stale until you switch tabs and back.
- PyQt mailing list: `QWebEnginePage.LifecycleState` does not behave as the C++ example does, i.e. PyQt freeze/thaw is unreliable.

These match the symptom exactly: input lost after the Frozen→Active round trip.

## Affected code

`qt_wrapper.py` `changeEvent`: `setLifecycleState(Frozen)` on `isMinimized()`, `Active` otherwise.

## Fix

Stop freezing. The freeze existed only to release memory while minimized, but the wrapper now has a gated renderer purge (`_purge_renderer`, issue #106) that frees memory **without** changing the lifecycle state. Keep the page `Active` (per Qt's "a visible page must remain Active") and purge on minimize instead; the ~1s purge stutter is invisible while minimized. No more Frozen→Active input loss.
title: UI unresponsive after minimize/restore: page freeze (setLifecycleState Frozen) loses input on thaw

body:
## Summary

Several CSS animations in the Brain (memory) and Notes panels generate raster tiles continuously. On Qt WebEngine the renderer never evicts tiles under memory pressure, so each perpetual animation is a steady, never-reclaimed contributor to memory and CPU growth while its panel is open.

The most costly is `memory-synapse-sweep`: a decorative shimmer on `#memory-list .memory-item::after` declared `infinite`, so it runs perpetually on every memory row (~20 rows = ~20 always-running animations) whenever the panel is open, whether or not the user is interacting. Measured: cancelling all running CSS animations dropped the idle renderer climb by ~1.7 MB/s, dominated by this one. Today it is also inverted: the sweep is hidden on hover (`:hover::after { opacity: 0 }`), i.e. it runs at rest and disappears when pointed at.

## Scope (branch `fix/brain-panel-oom`)

1. Compositor-promote the animations so they no longer force main-thread raster: `@property --sweep` -> `transform: translateX()`; remove `filter` from `note-ai-shine`; `animation:none` -> `animation-play-state:paused` on `notes-quick-add`; `background-position` -> `transform` in `notes-drag-shimmer`.
2. Make `memory-synapse-sweep` hover-triggered instead of perpetual: no animation at rest, one sweep on hover, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`. Compositor-promotion alone does not remove the cost of ~20 animations running forever; hover-gating does, while keeping the visual on the row the user points at.

## Why it matters

Self-hosted users on modest hardware: ~20 perpetual compositor animations per open panel is a continuous, never-reclaimed cost on an engine that does not evict tiles, and the effect adds nothing while the user is not looking at a specific row.
title: Brain/Notes panel CSS animations generate continuous raster tiles; compositor-promote and make memory sweep hover-triggered
Whirlpool spinner rAF loop never terminates when element is never appended (or is hidden): perpetual CPU + canvas churn

body:
## Summary

The renderer process grows unbounded (measured 5+ GB and climbing ~3 to 11 MB/s while idle with several panels open) and never reclaims, even though `qt_wrapper.py` already has a full reclaim system (periodic timer, mouse-idle eviction, focus-loss GC, minimize freeze). The reason: the load-bearing "tile eviction" call is `Memory.simulatePressureNotification('critical')`, which is a **no-op on this QtWebEngine build**. The triggers fire, but nothing is reclaimed.

## Evidence (live CDP, 2026-06-25)

- Renderer RSS holds the memory; JS heap only 43 MB; decoded images 47 MB.
- `Memory.simulatePressureNotification('critical')`: RSS 4861 to 4884 MB (no change).
- `Memory.forciblyPurgeJavaScriptMemory` (page target): RSS 4884 to 1141 MB, and in a separate test 6425 to 1179 MB. Reclaims multiple GB in one call.
- Pausing all CSS animations, clearing all timers, and hiding all panels each left the climb slope unchanged: this is diffuse renderer cache (raster tiles, transfer buffers, transient Oilpan), not a JS leak or one widget.

Root cause is the known QtWebEngine gap: it never forwards an OS memory-pressure signal to the renderer, so Chromium's eviction path never fires. The wrapper's existing `gc()` calls only collect the 43 MB JS/Oilpan pool, not the multi-GB renderer cache.

## Affected code

- `qt_wrapper.py` `_log_renderer_memory` (periodic): calls `simulatePressureNotification` (~line 619).
- `qt_wrapper.py` `_evict_on_idle` (mouse-idle 2s): same call (~line 690).
- `mac_wrapper.py` / `windows_wrapper.py`: same pattern, for parity.

## Fix (layer 3 of the memory architecture)

Replace `simulatePressureNotification('critical')` with `Memory.forciblyPurgeJavaScriptMemory` at the existing reclaim sites, with discipline:

- **Off the interaction path only.** A forcible purge causes a roughly 1 second stutter (still present; a different stutter was fixed in Session 4). Fire only on focus-loss, minimize, and deep idle, never while interacting or streaming.
- **RSS ceiling gate.** Only purge when renderer VmRSS is above a threshold (baseline after purge is ~1.1 GB), so light use never stutters.
- **Rate limited.** Minimum interval between purges so it cannot repeat back to back.
- **Off the main thread.** Run in the CDP executor so socket I/O does not add to the stall.

This bounds the renderer footprint while keeping the purge invisible to an active user.

## Scope

Layer 3 (reclaim) of the broader memory-management architecture in `docs/fork/memory-management-architecture.md`. Layers 2 (panel teardown-on-close / residency) and 1 (paint discipline) are separate follow-up issues. Upstream-candidate; the wrapper is fork-developed, so this branch stacks on the Qt native app feature branch.
title: Renderer memory climbs unbounded: reclaim calls simulatePressureNotification, a no-op on QtWebEngine (use forciblyPurgeJavaScriptMemory)

body:
## Summary

Chat image generation is effectively unreachable for a normal user, even though the backend tool works. Asking the chat to "generate an image" returns "I don't have that capability," and the Settings → **Image Generation** panel offers no usable way to fix it: it lists only hardcoded Stable Diffusion models shown as "(not detected)" and exposes no provider/model that can actually generate an image.

The tool itself is fine. The problem is configuration discoverability and a conflation between two different "image model" concepts.

## What actually happens

1. The `generate_image` tool exists and is wired end-to-end (`src/tool_policy.py:38`, `src/tool_index.py:91`, parser/executor in `src/tool_execution.py:332,354`, backend `do_generate_image` in `src/ai_interaction.py:877`).
2. It is gated off until `image_gen_enabled` is set: `src/agent_loop.py:1402` — `if not get_setting("image_gen_enabled", False): disabled.add("generate_image")`. Before enabling it, the model is never offered the tool, so it answers that it cannot generate images.
3. `do_generate_image` resolves a model by auto-detecting cloud image models (`gpt-image-1.5` > `gpt-image-1` > `dall-e-3`) and otherwise falling back to any enabled local endpoint with `model_type == "image"` (`src/ai_interaction.py:914-946`). With no such credential or endpoint configured, it has nothing to run.
4. The Settings → **Image Generation** panel (`static/js/settings.js` `initImageSettings`, ~line 742) is **scoped to inpainting**: it filters to inpaint-compatible Stable Diffusion models and appends hardcoded fallbacks (`stable-diffusion-3.5-medium`, `stable-diffusion-inpainting`) labelled "(not detected)" when none are served (`settings.js:751-773`). It does **not** list image-type endpoints, nor the cloud `gpt-image`/`dall-e` options.
5. That same panel writes the shared `image_model` setting (`settings.js:794`) — the exact key `do_generate_image` reads as its chat-generation default (`ai_interaction.py:910`). So selecting an (uninstalled) inpaint model there can also point chat generation at a model that does not resolve.

There **is** a real path to register an image endpoint — Admin → add a local endpoint with type **Image** (`static/index.html:2093-2094`, `adm-epLocalType`) — but nothing in the image-generation settings or the chat surface points a user there, and cloud `gpt-image`/`dall-e` requires a separately configured credential.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh install, no image endpoint configured and no cloud image credential.
2. Ask the chat to generate an image → "I don't have that capability."
3. Open Settings → Image Generation, enable it. The model selector offers only auto-detect plus `stable-diffusion-*` "(not detected)". There is no way to select a provider/model that can actually generate.
4. Generation still does not work, with no surfaced reason.

## Impact

A user cannot discover how to enable chat image generation. The one settings panel that appears to configure it is actually for editor inpainting, lists models they do not have, and silently shares its model setting with chat generation. When generation is enabled but unconfigured, the failure is silent (the model just says it cannot), with no message pointing at the missing image model/endpoint.

## Proposed direction (not final)

- Separate the **inpaint** model setting from the **chat image-generation** model setting, or clearly label the existing panel as inpaint-only.
- Make the image-generation settings list real options: registered `model_type=image` endpoints and the available cloud image models, instead of a hardcoded SD allowlist.
- When `image_gen_enabled` is true but no image model/endpoint resolves, surface a clear reason (e.g. "No image model configured — add an Image endpoint in Admin or configure a gpt-image/DALL·E credential") instead of failing silently.

## Classification

Upstream-candidate (product/UX fix). Branch from `upstream-mirror` when work starts. Not part of the chat stick-to-bottom work; filed so that track can stay separate.
title: Chat image generation is undiscoverable: settings are inpaint-scoped and don't expose a working provider/model

body:
## Bug

During streaming with auto-follow active, the view fails to stay snapped to the bottom across the "Thinking" placeholder transition. The `.agent-thinking-dots` box appears (grows content, snaps to bottom), then is removed before the real message renders (content shrinks), then the message appears (content grows). The view ends up stuck above the bottom instead of re-attaching.

## Root cause (`static/js/ui.js`, `static/js/chat.js`)

- `scrollHistory()` is throttled: `if (_scrollThrottleTimer) return;` only starts a new scroll animation every 500ms. The grow/shrink/grow happens within that window, so the re-snap after the message renders is dropped.
- `_removeThinkingSpinner` removes the box but does not re-snap.
- `_smoothScrollStep` stops once it reaches the bottom (`diff <= 1`), so no animation is running to follow the later grow; and its `maxAllowedDiff` guard bails on large grows.

## Fix

Add a short "settle" loop (`scrollHistorySettle`) that, when auto-follow is enabled, snaps to the bottom every frame for ~350ms, tracking the moving bottom across the transition, bypassing the streaming throttle. Call it when the Thinking spinner is removed so the subsequent message grow is followed. Gated on `autoScrollEnabled` so a user who scrolled up is never yanked down.

Part of the #2 plan (item 3.2). Lays the groundwork for 3.3 (Thinking-as-overlay), which removes the layout transition entirely.

## Test

Source-text assertions that `scrollHistorySettle` exists, is gated on `autoScrollEnabled`, snaps each frame for a bounded window, and is called from `_removeThinkingSpinner`.

comments.body: The one remaining unverified path is now behaviorally confirmed (2026-07-18, real app): the per-child ResizeObserver leg. (a) pinned + late 600px child growth (highlight-reflow/image-decode shape) → re-pins; (b) pinned + shrink-then-grow (Thinking transition shape, 900px) → re-pins; (c) scrolled-up viewport + same growth → position held within 4px, no yank. Probe: scratchpad probe_32.py shape — establish pin via real scroll, mutate a rendered child's layout, assert bottom-distance. With this, plan item 3.2 (snap-to-bottom hardening) is verified complete; the fix itself has been this branch's observer all along.

title: fix(chat): snap-to-bottom drops out across the Thinking-box grow/shrink/grow transition

body:
## Bug

In the chat-history virtualization (`fix/dom-oom-virtualization`, #2), scrolling **up** correctly loads one batch of older messages and prunes the bottom, preserving scroll position. Scrolling **down** should be the inverse (load one batch of newer messages, prune the top, preserve position), but instead it behaves like the "scroll to bottom" button: it loads every remaining batch and snaps to the newest message.

## Root cause

In `MessageWindow.prototype._loadNewer` (`static/js/chatHistory.js`), the rAF continuation recurses when `self._draining || self._isAtBottom()`. `_isAtBottom()` is a 120px proximity check, and scrolling down to bring the bottom sentinel into view (which triggers the load) puts the viewport within that 120px. So `_isAtBottom()` is true and the load recurses batch after batch to the end, then snaps to the bottom. The `_draining` flag exists to distinguish the button (drain all) from a scroll (load one), but `|| _isAtBottom()` defeats it. The reached-end branch also snaps to the bottom unconditionally.

## Fix

- Recurse only when `_draining` (button). A scroll loads exactly one batch and stops; the next loads when the user scrolls the bottom sentinel back into view, mirroring `_loadOlder`.
- The reached-end snap and settle loop run only when draining, so a scroll that reaches the newest message stops at the user's position instead of yanking to the bottom.
- Wording: the bottom sentinel says "earlier messages"; scroll-down loads newer messages. Correct to "newer".

Part of the #2 plan (`docs/fork/plans/dom-oom-virtualization-upstream-plan.md`, item 3.1).

## Test

Regression test asserting the `_loadNewer` recursion and the reached-end snap are gated on `_draining` (not `_isAtBottom()`), plus the bottom-sentinel wording.

comments.body:
**Verified fixed — and the verification caught a fresh regression on top of it (#132).**

The fix this issue prescribes has been in the code since 2026-06-25 (`8fc0dcdc`, cherry-picked from the staging branch): `_loadNewer`'s rAF continuation gates on `_draining` only, the reached-end snap and settle loop are drain-only, and the bottom sentinel says "newer messages". All three have static guards (`test_load_newer_recursion_gated_on_draining_only`, `test_load_newer_end_snap_is_drain_only`, `test_bottom_sentinel_says_newer_not_earlier`), and yesterday's convergence (`463526b0`) carried them to the staged #2 branch. The issue was simply never updated when the fix landed.

Real-app behavioral verification (n=600, deep scroll-up then scroll-down trigger, post-#127 spacer geometry) initially FAILED — 125 messages on one trigger — which turned out to be a new, separate defect introduced by the #127 bottom spacer (batch inserted below the spacer; filed and fixed as #132). With #132 fixed, the measured behavior is exactly this issue's requirement: one trigger loads one batch (`_endIdx` 80 → 105), stops, no drain, no yank to bottom, position held.

Upstream-candidate — stays open until #2's PR is filed (plan item 3.1 is marked done pending that filing).

title: fix(chatHistory): scroll-down drains to bottom instead of acting as the inverse of scroll-up

body:
## Goal

Let a reopened editor draft restore its undo history so the user can keep undoing after closing/reopening the app. Today `state.undoStack` is reset to `[]` on every editor open (galleryEditor.js), so reopening restores the current edited image but no history.

## Cost analysis (why NOT full history)

The draft payload already stores each layer as a base64 PNG. Undo snapshots store every layer's/mask's/wand's full pixels per step (≤ MAX_HISTORY=20). Flattened photographic layers **do not compress** (measured under #99: gzip ratio ≈ 0.997 on photo-noise). So persisting the *full* stack ≈ **20× the full-image payload written on every debounced save** during editing — tens-to-hundreds of MB through the SQLite TEXT `payload` column and over the remote tunnel the save path is tuned to keep small. That's a save-latency + DB-bloat regression, not a tradeoff. **Full history is rejected.**

## Recommended scope: bounded tail

- Persist the last **N** undo steps (e.g. 8), capped to a **total compressed-size budget** (e.g. ~6 MB), whichever hits first.
- Reuse #99's gzip codec; serialize each snapshot's pixel slots (layers/masks/wand) as gzip→base64 in a new draft payload field. **Clone-and-compress** — do NOT mutate the live stack (that would convert #99's recent raw snapshots and break in-session sync undo).
- Draft schema `v2 → v3`, backward-compatible (no `undo` field = current behavior).
- Restore rebuilds `state.undoStack` with `_gz` set + `_compressed=true`; #99's `_decompressSnap` decodes on demand.

## Why deferred

~200 lines of correctness-critical async serialization touching draft persistence; cross-session restore is **untestable without driving the live editor**. Warrants its own session. Depends on #99 (`perf/editor-undo-compress`) — branch from there, not upstream-mirror.

## Acceptance

- Reopening a draft restores a bounded undo tail; undo works back through it.
- Draft save payload stays bounded (size budget enforced); no save-latency regression.
- Old `v2` drafts load unchanged.
- Live smoke-test: edit → close → reopen → undo the last few steps; deep-undo pixels identical (gzip is lossless).

comments.body: **Upstream reconciliation:** serves ROADMAP.md "Expand the Editor for quicker, more robust everyday use… stronger image handling." No existing upstream issue/PR on cross-session editor undo persistence found — net-new. Depends on #99.

title: feat(editor): persist undo history across sessions (bounded; deferred)

body:
## Bug

Saving from the gallery photo editor can create a **0-byte gallery image** (null×null dimensions) — a broken entry in the gallery. Observed: a 0-byte `*.jpg` appeared next to the source photo after an edit session.

## Root cause

Both save paths flatten + encode + upload with **no guard against an empty result**:
- `ge-save` (replace original): `flatten() → toBlob() → POST /api/gallery/<id>/replace`
- `exportToGallery` (save copy): `flatten() → toBlob() → POST /api/gallery/upload`

`flatten()` builds a canvas of `state.imgWidth × state.imgHeight`. If those are 0/unset (e.g. a save firing before the image is fully loaded, or after a state reset), the flattened canvas is 0×0 and the upload writes an empty file — the server stores a 0-byte image with null dimensions. `toBlob`'s existing null-check doesn't catch a valid-but-empty encode.

## Fix

A shared guard used by both paths:
- Refuse to encode if the flattened canvas has zero width/height.
- Refuse to upload if the resulting blob is empty / trivially small.
- Surface an error toast instead of silently creating a broken entry (the existing try/catch already shows errors).

## Test

Source-text guards asserting both save handlers validate canvas dimensions and blob size before upload.

comments.body: **Upstream reconciliation:** fits upstream tracking issue #2125 ("Front-end editor and rendering bugs" — each fixed by a PR with a regression test); this empty-save guard matches that pattern (`tests/test_editor_empty_save_guard.py`). Directly serves ROADMAP.md: "Expand the Editor… clearer save/export flows." When filed upstream, link under #2125.

title: fix(editor): editor save can create a 0-byte broken gallery image (no empty-output guard)

body:
## Bug

In the gallery photo editor, **Ctrl+Shift+Z does nothing** (redo). Redo itself works (the toolbar button and history panel), only the keyboard shortcut is dead.

## Root cause

`static/js/editor/keyboard-shortcuts.js` (~line 88):

```js
if (e.key === 'z') { e.preventDefault(); if (e.shiftKey) redo(); else undo(); }
```

When Shift is held, `e.key` for the Z key is the **uppercase `'Z'`**, so `e.key === 'z'` is false and the `redo()` branch is never reached. Plain Ctrl+Z (no shift) works because `e.key` is lowercase `'z'`.

The rest of the file already handles this — e.g. `(e.key === 'D' || e.key === 'd')` and `(e.key === 's' || e.key === 'S')`. The redo line is the lone case-sensitive one.

## Fix

```js
if (e.key === 'z' || e.key === 'Z') { e.preventDefault(); if (e.shiftKey) redo(); else undo(); }
```

Aesthetics-neutral; restores the documented 'Ctrl+Z undo (Shift adds redo)' behavior.

## Test

Source-text guard asserting the undo/redo chord accepts both `'z'` and `'Z'`.

comments.body: **Upstream reconciliation:** fits upstream tracking issue #2125 ("Front-end editor and rendering bugs" — distinct front-end bugs, each fixed by a linked PR with a regression test). This redo-shortcut fix follows that exact pattern (one focused bug + `tests/test_editor_redo_shortcut.py`). When filed upstream, link/add it under #2125. Also serves ROADMAP.md item "Expand the Editor… clearer save/export flows."

title: fix(editor): Ctrl+Shift+Z (redo) shortcut dead — e.key is 'Z' uppercase when Shift held

body:
## Summary

The gallery photo-editor's undo system (`galleryEditor._snapshotState`) stores **every layer's full raw `getImageData`** (plus masks + wand) on every mutating op, kept up to `MAX_HISTORY = 20`. Bounded and freed on editor close, but the transient peak during an active multi-layer/large-image session can reach hundreds of MB to GBs.

Reduce the peak by **PNG-compressing snapshots** (lossless — no pixel corruption risk), while keeping full undo depth.

## Design (recent-raw hybrid, to contain async risk)

- Keep the most recent N snapshots **raw** (`ImageData`) so the common 'undo last action' stays synchronous and instant.
- Compress snapshots that fall outside the raw window in `requestIdleCallback` (off the edit critical path): `ImageData → PNG dataURL` via a temp canvas; free the raw buffer.
- `_restoreState` becomes async **only** when the target snapshot is compressed: decode all `_png` (layers/masks/wand) via `Image.onload`, then run the existing sync apply + `composite()`. A `_restoreGen` counter (bumped per undo/redo) discards stale decodes if a newer undo/redo started.

## Why lossless / no corruption risk

PNG is lossless; round-trip pixels are identical. Unlike structural-sharing (rejected — ~200 diffuse mutation sites, no safe dirty-flag), there is no shared-reference or dirty-tracking hazard.

## Cost

Deep-undo latency (decode of a compressed snapshot) — a *visible, recoverable* cost, never silent corruption. Recent undo unaffected. Capture unaffected (compression is deferred to idle).

## Testing

Synchronous logic (compress/decompress round-trip, raw-window bookkeeping, gen-guard structure) is unit-tested. **Async undo/redo race behavior requires a live editor smoke-test** before landing (edit → deep undo → redo → crop-undo across layers + masks + wand). Branch must not cherry-pick to develop until that passes.

## Follow-up

`notes.js` keeps 30 full `ImageData` snapshots — same technique applies, separate change.

comments.body:
**Codec changed PNG → gzip during implementation.** A PNG round-trip via canvas (`putImageData→toDataURL`, `drawImage→getImageData`) passes through the canvas's *premultiplied* alpha and can drift partial-alpha pixels by ±1/channel (soft brushes, feathered masks) — which would violate the lossless/no-corruption property this approach was chosen for. `CompressionStream('gzip')` over the raw `ImageData` bytes is byte-exact (DEFLATE is lossless) and never touches a canvas, and it's async (matches the deep-undo restore path). If `CompressionStream` is unavailable it no-ops (snapshots stay raw; undo still works).

Implemented on `perf/editor-undo-compress` (`3a310c9b`). **Held off develop** pending a live editor smoke-test (async undo/redo races + gzip round-trip can't be auto-tested without the editor UI). 10 source-text contract guards in `tests/test_editor_undo_compression.py`.

**Upstream reconciliation:** serves ROADMAP.md item "Expand the Editor for quicker, more robust everyday use… stronger image handling" (bounds the editor's transient undo-memory peak). No existing upstream issue/PR found specifically on editor undo-snapshot memory; this would be net-new. Related family: the browser-memory work under #4644.

title: perf(editor): PNG-compress older undo snapshots to cut edit-session memory peak

body: ## Summary Off-screen images in stacked/grid layouts decode into memory eagerly. Add `loading="lazy"` + `decoding="async"` to the renderers that produce many off-screen images at once, so they decode near-viewport and off the main thread. ## Scope (per-site, deliberately narrow) Most image sites are already handled or don't benefit: - Gallery main grids (`gallery.js` ~572/1219) **already** set `loading="lazy"`. - Chat-history images are covered by DOM virtualization (off-screen nodes pruned). - Detail/focus/lightbox images (`gallery.js` ~1397 `#gallery-detail-img`, `chatRenderer` overlay) must stay **eager** — they're the user's focus; lazy would delay them. Genuine net-new wins (many images rendered at once, most off-screen): - **Document page stack** (`document.js` ~1169): a multi-page document renders as a vertical stack of full-page PNGs — every page decodes at once today. Strongest case. - **Gallery draft thumbnails** (`gallery.js` ~914 `.gallery-editor-draft-thumb`): a grid of draft thumbs. ## Change - Document page ``: `img.loading = 'lazy'; img.decoding = 'async';` - Draft-thumb template: add `loading="lazy"`. ## Why aesthetics are unchanged `loading="lazy"` only defers decode/load for images outside the viewport; on-screen images are unaffected. `decoding="async"` moves decode off the main thread (no visual change, less jank). No layout, color, or animation change. ## Acceptance - Document page images and gallery draft thumbs carry `loading="lazy"` (+ `decoding="async"` where created in JS). - Focus/detail images remain eager. - Static-analysis test asserts the attributes on the page/thumb renderers.

comments.body:
**Upstream reconciliation (relates to #4852):** upstream issue #4852 ("serve thumbnails in the grid instead of full-resolution originals", filed the same day) is the proper fix for the main gallery **grid** memory problem — server-side cached thumbnails (~400px WebP), citing Immich. It explicitly notes that **client-side `loading="lazy"`/`decoding="async"` does not help the grid**, because each visible tile still downloads and decodes the full-res original; only a server thumbnail avoids the transfer+decode.

This issue (#98) targets **different surfaces** and is complementary: the document multi-page PNG stack (a genuine client-side win — #4852 doesn't cover documents) and the gallery *draft* thumbnails (already small generated JPEGs, so lazy/async there is harmless but low-value). #98 does **not** solve the gallery-grid problem; #4852 does. Recommend supporting/co-filing #4852's server-thumbnail approach for the grid, and narrowing #98's framing to the document-page win.

title: perf(ui): lazy-decode off-screen stacked/grid images (document pages, gallery draft thumbs)

body:
## Summary

Hovering interactive UI (memory list, sidebar nav, etc.) steadily grows renderer memory during idle use. Root cause: CSS `:hover` pseudo-elements (`::before`/`::after`) are real DOM `Node`s created on hover-enter and destroyed on leave — legitimate transient churn — but QtWebEngine never fires Oilpan GC during idle pointer activity, so the garbage accumulates until a chat response triggers the existing post-response `gc()`.

## Diagnosis (evidence)

- Hover-storm (real `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`) over Brain memory items: +2841 DOM nodes over 12 rounds, monotonic; `gc()` returns to baseline. Listeners flat (+0 — no listener leak).
- Region isolation: items/sidebar churn heavily (+1700/+1500 per 800 moves), modal header barely (+208) → tracks interactive elements with hover styles.
- Live node count flat while total grows → detachment (pseudo-element create/destroy).
- Heap snapshot shows 0 retained detached nodes (its implicit GC sweeps them → trivially collectable, not a retention leak). V8 allocation profiler empty → native Blink nodes, no JS producer.
- **Disabling author CSS collapses churn +1676 → +182** → confirmed CSS-driven; no single JS handler to fix.

## Fix

Idle-triggered **async** `gc({type:'major',execution:'async'})`, debounced like the existing post-response GC (chat.js ~3248), fired after a short window of pointer inactivity while focused. Async + debounced to avoid the gray-frame flicker and not fight the focus-loss GC timer. Not a handler fix — stripping hover pseudo-elements would remove legitimate UI.

## Acceptance

- After sustained hovering with no chat activity, an idle GC fires and reclaims the churn (RSS/node count return toward baseline).
- Regression guard test: listeners stay flat and node count reclaims after `gc()` (Playwright integration harness).
- No flicker; no conflict with focus-loss GC.

comments.body: **Upstream reconciliation:** relates to upstream issue #4644 ("browser tab OOM during long agent interactions"). The open upstream PR #4661 addresses #4644 by reducing DOM *production* (server-paginated history, 'show older' bar, plain-text thinking-block streaming). This idle-GC is **complementary** — it reclaims transient Oilpan garbage (CSS `:hover` pseudo-elements) during idle interaction, a source #4661 doesn't touch. No overlap/conflict. PR draft updated to position against #4644/#4661. (Separately: the fork's DOM-virtualization #2 *does* overlap #4661 and needs maintainer coordination.)

title: perf(qt): idle-triggered GC to reclaim transient hover DOM churn (CSS :hover pseudo-elements)

body:
## Summary

Remove `--enable-low-end-device-mode` from the Qt wrapper flags. Controlled experiments show it (a) causes a visible lighter-rectangle raster tint on dark themes and (b) does **not** bound the memory problem it was added for.

## Evidence

- **Tint cause, proven by on/off toggle:** with the flag, a faint lighter band (`#1e1e2e` → `#222233`, tile-aligned) appears over the content area; removing it makes all sampled pixels read `#1e1e2e`. It's the flag's low-fidelity raster *path*, not an eviction fill — `page.setBackgroundColor()` is already `#1e1e2e` and has no effect on it; `--disable-low-res-tiling` doesn't fix it either.
- **Doesn't bound the OOM:** the real growth (hovering UI items) is transient Oilpan DOM-node churn from CSS `:hover` pseudo-elements — a *separate memory pool* from raster tiles. Capping raster (~96 MB) does nothing for it. Measured: hover node growth is identical with the flag on; fully reclaimed by `gc()`.

## Fix

Drop the flag. No raster cap replacement (raster was never the problem). The hover-OOM is addressed separately by idle-triggered GC (see companion issue). Keep `page.setBackgroundColor(_theme_bg_color())` (harmless correct base color) but remove the test assertions that encoded the disproven eviction-fill rationale.

## Acceptance

- Flag removed from all wrappers (qt/mac/windows).

body:
## Summary

Make the Odysseus server optionally reachable over the network so users can run the server on one machine and use it from a tablet, phone, or laptop via that device's native browser — no desktop wrapper required on the client.

## Background

Odysseus is two runtimes: (1) the FastAPI web app (the product, already responsive — `@media (max-width: 768px)` breakpoints exist), and (2) the optional Qt desktop wrapper that embeds Chromium and points at localhost. A remote tablet uses runtime (1) directly through its own browser (Safari/Chrome), which is fully OS-managed — so none of the wrapper's memory/raster workarounds apply, and rendering is correct out of the box.

The blocker today: the wrapper launches uvicorn with `--host 127.0.0.1` (qt_wrapper.py), so the server is unreachable from any other device.

## Scope

- **Binding.** Opt-in network bind (e.g. `0.0.0.0` or a configured interface) instead of hardcoded `127.0.0.1`. Must remain localhost-only by default.
- **Auth.** Network exposure requires authentication. Audit the existing api-token infrastructure and the `127.0.0.1`/`::1` trust checks in app.py (forwarded-header handling already exists, suggesting reverse-proxy/tunnel was anticipated).
- **TLS.** Document/support TLS, whether direct or via reverse proxy.
- **CORS.** `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is env-configurable; verify it composes with network access.

## Non-goals

- No Chromium/engine work — this is entirely server-side. The client renders in its own browser.

## Acceptance

- Server can be made LAN-reachable via explicit opt-in, localhost-only by default.
- Authentication required when network-exposed.
- TLS path documented.
- Responsive UI verified on a tablet form factor.
title: feat(server): network-reachable mode for remote access from tablets and other devices

body:
## Summary

Expose `--enable-low-end-device-mode` as an opt-in preference for the desktop Qt wrapper, so users on genuinely low-end PCs can trade raster fidelity for a bounded ~96 MB `cc::TileManager` budget, while everyone else runs at full fidelity by default.

## Background

The flag is currently always-on in the wrapper as a workaround for QtWebEngine not receiving OS memory-pressure signals (see #67, #14). It has a visual cost: low-end mode also enables low-resolution raster tiling, which renders some tiles ~+4/+4/+5 lighter, producing a faint lighter rectangle over the content area on dark themes (e.g. Catppuccin `#1e1e2e` → `#222233`). Confirmed by controlled experiment: disabling the flag removes the tint entirely; `page.setBackgroundColor()` does **not** affect it (it is a raster-path artifact, not an eviction fill).

## Constraints (important)

- **Startup-only.** `--enable-low-end-device-mode` is a Chromium *launch* switch — it cannot be toggled live in the web UI. The preference must be read at wrapper startup (same pattern as `_theme_bg_color()` reading `data/user_prefs.json`), and changing it requires an app restart. The settings UI must communicate the restart requirement.
- **Scope: PCs only.** Only machines running the wrapper are affected. Low-end tablets remote in via their own native browser, which self-manages memory and needs no flag.
- **Must bundle the tint fix.** The 'on' state must not reintroduce the lighter rectangle — ship the raster-tint fix together with the toggle (tracked separately).
- **Default: off.** Full fidelity for the common case.

## Acceptance

- Wrapper reads a `low_end_mode` preference at startup and conditionally appends the flag.
- Settings UI exposes the toggle with a clear 'requires restart' note.
- 'On' state is visually correct (no lighter rectangle).
- Static-analysis tests in `tests/test_qt_cdp_listener_audit.py`.

comments.body:
### Discoverability requirement

The toggle must be **visible in the settings menu unconditionally**, even though it is restart-gated. Two reasons:

1. **Awareness.** Users can't choose an option they don't know exists. A restart-gated control is still worth surfacing — the 'takes effect next launch' note sets the right expectation without hiding the feature.
2. **Performance-over-aesthetics is a legitimate preference.** Some users on weaker hardware will happily accept reduced raster fidelity (and the faint lighter banding, if the tint fix can't fully eliminate it on their config) in exchange for the bounded tile budget and smoother behavior. That trade should be theirs to make, presented plainly in the UI — not decided for them by hiding the flag.

So: always render the toggle in settings; annotate with the restart requirement; default off.

Closing: premise falsified by diagnosis. The toggle would expose `--enable-low-end-device-mode`, but controlled tests show that flag (a) causes the lighter-rectangle raster tint and (b) does NOT bound the hover-OOM — which is transient Oilpan DOM churn from CSS `:hover` pseudo-elements, a separate pool from raster tiles. There is no useful 'low-end mode' to toggle here. The real fixes are tracked in the two companion issues (drop the flag; idle-triggered GC). Remote access is tracked separately in #95.

title: feat(qt): opt-in low-end-device-mode toggle (startup pref) for the desktop wrapper

body:
## Problem

`contain: content` (which includes `contain: paint`) was added to `.sidebar` and `.chat-history` in commit b6f0f941. This causes two distinct visual bugs:

**Bug 1 — Sidebar backdrop-filter broken (frosted theme)**

`.sidebar` + `contain: paint` conflicts with `body.theme-frosted #sidebar { backdrop-filter: blur(24px) }`. When an element has paint containment and is composited into its own layer, `backdrop-filter` reads from the element's own layer context rather than the composited background behind it. The frosted glass effect on the sidebar either renders incorrectly or fails to blur the background.

**Bug 2 — Transparent chat area renders opaque (Qt WebEngine)**

`.chat-history` + `contain: paint` + `overflow-y: auto` promotes the element to an independent compositor layer. In Qt WebEngine with `--enable-low-end-device-mode` (small tile budget), compositor tiles for the chat-history layer use a solid background color when tiles are evicted or regenerated. Since `.chat-history` has no CSS background, this shows as an opaque solid color instead of the transparent body background (canvas animation, dots pattern, etc.) the user expects to see.

The user sees the canvas/CSS background incorrectly (or not at all) behind the main working area and the right-side sidebar.

## Root cause

`contain: paint` is correct for elements that need paint isolation (clipping, independent stacking context for repaint bounding). It is **not safe** for:
- Elements that use `backdrop-filter` (or that will have `backdrop-filter` applied via theme rules)
- Transparent elements in a composited rendering pipeline where the background must show through

## Fix

Change both elements from `contain: content` to `contain: layout style`:

```css
/* Before (broken) */
.sidebar    { contain: content; }
.chat-history { contain: content; }

/* After (correct) */
.sidebar      { contain: layout style; }
.chat-history { contain: layout style; }
```

`contain: layout style` retains:
- Layout isolation (style recalculations scoped to the subtree)
- Style isolation (counter/quote propagation blocked)

Without:
- Paint containment (no stacking context from contain, no compositor layer promotion via paint)

This matches the existing `.modal-content` pattern which uses `contain: layout style` specifically because it must not create paint clipping (provider picker menus overflow the modal boundary).

## Branch

`fix/css-contain-paint-transparent-rendering` from `upstream-mirror`

## Affected files

- `static/style.css` — change contain values on `.sidebar` and `.chat-history`
- `tests/test_css_render_perf.py` — update assertions to match new contain values
title: fix(css): contain:paint on sidebar and chat-history breaks backdrop-filter and transparent compositing
fix(css): global hover raster tile accumulation — containment, animation, and transition fixes

body:
## Problem

The current `_log_renderer_memory` in `qt_wrapper.py` reports renderer process RSS and cc::TileManager DOM counts but provides no visibility into:

1. How much of RSS is V8 heap vs Blink vs Skia — needed to determine whether tile eviction or GC is the right intervention at any given moment.
2. Python/Qt host process RSS — the full memory picture requires both renderer and host.

Without V8 heap breakdown, it is impossible to know whether memory pressure is coming from compositor tiles (fixed by `Memory.simulatePressureNotification`) or V8 heap (fixed by `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage`).

## Fix

**1. Add `Runtime.getHeapUsage` to `_log_renderer_memory`:**

```python
heap = _cdp_call('Runtime.getHeapUsage', {})
if heap:
    used  = heap.get('usedSize',  0) // (1024 * 1024)
    total = heap.get('totalSize', 0) // (1024 * 1024)
    print(f'[V8] heap: used={used} MB total={total} MB', flush=True)
```

**2. Add `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage` to the idle mouse eviction path:**

When the user has been idle for 2 seconds, fire `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage` (synchronous V8+Oilpan GC) alongside `Memory.simulatePressureNotification` (cc::TileManager eviction). Together these address both compositor and V8 heap accumulation during hover.

**3. Log host process RSS:**

Read `/proc/self/status` VmRSS and log it alongside the renderer RSS:

```
[MEM] host RSS: 853 MB  renderer RSS: 851 MB
```

## Scope

- `qt_wrapper.py` (Linux) — branch `feat/qt-native-linux-app`, extends issue #14
- `mac_wrapper.py` (macOS) — branch `feat/qt-native-macos-app`
- `windows_wrapper.py` (Windows) — branch `feat/qt-native-windows-app`

## Research

See `docs/fork/memory-explosion-research.md` Session 9 — Phase 1 and Phase 2A (HeapProfiler).
title: perf(qt): add V8 heap telemetry, HeapProfiler.collectGarbage, and host-process RSS logging

body:
## Problem

Qt's `QTWEBENGINE_CHROMIUM_FLAGS` environment variable is parsed by splitting on spaces with no quoting support. The current `--js-flags` entry in `qt_wrapper.py`, `mac_wrapper.py`, and `windows_wrapper.py`:

```python
"--js-flags=--expose-gc --initial-old-space-size=128 --max-old-space-size=512 --optimize-for-size --minor-mc",
```

Qt sees this as 5 separate tokens. Only `--js-flags=--expose-gc` (no spaces in the value) reaches V8. The remaining 4 flags are passed to the renderer as bare Chromium switches and silently ignored.

**Confirmed from live renderer `/proc/PID/cmdline`:** `--js-flags=--expose-gc` only — all V8 heap sizing flags absent.

**Effect:** V8 runs with default heap limits (~1.5–2 GB on a 16+ GB system). The V8 heap grows to 850+ MB from interactive hover without triggering GC. RSS grows from ~320 MB to ~607 MB+ just from mousing over UI elements.

## Fix

Switch to comma-separated V8 multi-flag syntax (no spaces):

```python
# qt_wrapper.py, mac_wrapper.py, windows_wrapper.py
"--js-flags=--expose-gc,--initial-old-space-size=128,--max-old-space-size=512,--optimize-for-size,--minor-mc",
```

V8 accepts `--js-flags=a,b,c` as equivalent to `--js-flags a --js-flags b --js-flags c`. No spaces means Qt cannot split the value.

Also add `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage` CDP call to the idle mouse eviction path (alongside the existing `Memory.simulatePressureNotification`) for synchronous V8+Oilpan GC when the user has been idle for 2 seconds.

## Scope

- `qt_wrapper.py` (Linux)
- `mac_wrapper.py` (macOS)
- `windows_wrapper.py` (Windows)

## Research

See `docs/fork/memory-explosion-research.md` Session 9 — Root cause 1.
title: fix(qt): --js-flags space-splitting drops all V8 flags except --expose-gc

body:
## Summary

The Brain panel memory list grows RSS unbounded during hover interaction and does not reclaim memory after the panel closes. ~956 MiB RSS observed; closing the panel does not reduce it.

## Root causes (in order of impact)

**1. document.addEventListener accumulation (critical)**
`renderMemoryList()` adds one `document.addEventListener('click', ..., { once: false })` for every memory item on every render pass (line 956). With 50 items and 10 renders, 500 persistent document-level listeners accumulate, each holding a closure over a dropdown DOM element. These are never removed. Zero `removeEventListener` calls exist anywhere in memory.js (51 add / 0 remove).

**2. No event listener cleanup on re-render**
`memoryList.innerHTML = ''` at line 685 destroys the old item DOM nodes, but all their event listeners remain alive in memory until the GC happens to collect them. Because Qt does not forward OS memory pressure, that GC never fires during normal use.

**3. Animations run when modal is hidden**
All `::after` sweep animations on memory items continue running when `#memory-modal` gains `.hidden`. The compositor keeps raster tiles allocated for all items (including off-screen). Qt never evicts them.

**4. No cleanup or GC trigger on panel close**
Closing the Brain modal only toggles `.hidden`. No event listeners are released, no open dropdowns are removed, no GC is triggered.

## Fix

- Add an `AbortController` scoped to each `renderMemoryList()` call. Abort the previous controller before re-rendering to release all item listener closures before the DOM is cleared. Thread `{ signal }` through all 14 item-level addEventListener calls.
- Move the `document.addEventListener` for outside-click dropdown close inside the `menuBtn.click` handler with `{ once: true, signal }` — eliminates per-render accumulation and ensures it fires at most once per dropdown open.
- Add a `MutationObserver` on `#memory-modal` that runs cleanup (close open dropdown, abort controller, trigger GC) when the modal becomes hidden.
- CSS: add `animation-play-state: paused` when `#memory-modal.hidden` to stop all compositor animation work while the panel is not visible.
- Add `odysseus:modal-closed` CustomEvent in modalManager.js (parallel to existing `odysseus:modal-opened`).

body:
## Summary

Scrolling the mouse over the Brain memory list while items enter and leave hover state causes continuous raster-tile accumulation. Around 1 GB of growth is reproducible from repeated up-down scroll passes.

## Root causes

**1. `transition: all 0.15s` on `.memory-item` (base class, line 10844)**

The base class applies `transition: all` to every `.memory-item`. In the `#memory-list` scroll context, as the cursor moves over items during scroll each item cycles through enter-hover and leave-hover, animating `background` and `border-color` transitions. Both properties require main-thread painting (neither is compositor-promoted). At 60 fps with a 0.15 s transition that is 9 paint frames per enter/leave cycle, per item. Qt does not forward OS memory pressure to the embedded Chromium renderer; the raster tiles deposited by these transitions are never evicted.

**2. `will-change: transform` on all `#memory-list .memory-item::after` (line 10885)**

`will-change: transform` pre-promotes every `::after` pseudo-element to a compositor layer, including items scrolled off-screen. A continuously running `transform` animation auto-promotes the layer without this hint, so the declaration is redundant for visible items and actively harmful for off-screen ones: it forces GPU backing texture allocation for every item in the DOM regardless of viewport position.

## Fix

1. Override `transition: all 0.15s` in the `#memory-list .memory-item` context with `transition: opacity 0.15s` — limits transitions to compositor-promoted properties only. No raster tiles from scroll-triggered hover changes.

2. Remove `will-change: transform` from `#memory-list .memory-item::after` — the animation auto-promotes the layer when active; off-screen items do not need backing textures.

## Classification

Upstream-candidate. Same root cause as the fix in PR draft at `docs/fork/upstream/pr-drafts/fix-brain-panel-oom.md`: Qt not forwarding OS memory pressure means raster tiles from main-thread paint operations accumulate indefinitely.

body:
## Problem

The skill retrieval layer in `services/memory/skills.py:get_relevant_skills()` uses Jaccard token similarity. Jaccard treats all tokens equally — a query for "configure libvirt xml bridge networking" produces the same term weight for "configure" as for "libvirt". Skills with distinctive procedural vocabulary (specific tool names, domain terms, library names) are systematically under-retrieved when the query uses overlapping but not identical terminology.

Per SkillRet (arxiv:2605.05726, 2025) and the Skill Retrieval Benchmark (arxiv:2604.24594, 2025), hybrid BM25 + Jaccard significantly outperforms pure Jaccard for procedural skill retrieval. BM25 weights distinctive tokens higher, which is exactly what procedural skills need — a skill called "configure-libvirt-xml-networking" has vocabulary that should score high for targeted queries even with low raw overlap.

Additionally, Odysseus has five SkillOps diagnostic signals (arxiv:2605.13716, 2025) for each skill already stored in SKILL.md frontmatter and `_usage.json` sidecars — `confidence`, `audit_verdict`, `uses`, `necessity.necessary` — but no aggregated quality view. There's no way to quickly identify which skills are healthy vs. neglected without reading individual files.

## Proposed Fix

### BM25 Hybrid Retrieval (`services/memory/skills.py`)

Add `_compute_idf()` and `_bm25_score()` helpers at module level (near `_jaccard` and `_tokenize`). Modify `get_relevant_skills()` to compute a hybrid score: `0.5 * jaccard + 0.5 * bm25_norm`, where `bm25_norm = bm25_raw / (bm25_raw + 3.0)` (sigmoid-like normalization). Apply existing boosts unchanged on top.

Cache IDF on `SkillsManager._idf_cache`; invalidate in `add_skill()`, `update_skill()`, `delete_skill()`. IDF computation is O(N) over the skill corpus — caching eliminates per-request recomputation.

### Composite Health Score (`services/memory/skills.py`)

Add `_health_score(skill)` function returning a 0-100 integer from existing sidecar fields, calibrated to SkillOps five diagnostic dimensions:
- Confidence: 0-40 pts
- Audit verdict: pass=30, inconclusive=15, needs_work=10, skipped=5, fail=0 pts
- Usage (uses): 0-20 pts, log-scaled to 20 uses
- Necessity: +10 pts if necessary (or unknown — assume necessary for unaudited skills)

Add `"health_score": _health_score(result)` to `Skill.to_dict()`. This propagates automatically through all API endpoints that already call `to_dict()`.

### UI Badge (`static/js/skills.js`)

Add a color-coded health score badge on Brain > Skills cards (green ≥ 80, yellow 60-79, red < 60) with "Health: N/100" tooltip alongside the existing confidence % display.

## Research Basis

- **SkillRet** (arxiv:2605.05726, 2025): BM25 hybrid retrieval significantly outperforms Jaccard for procedural skill matching
- **Skill Retrieval Benchmark** (arxiv:2604.24594, 2025): distinctive vocabulary (tool names, domain terms) is the primary differentiator; BM25 weights these correctly
- **SkillOps** (arxiv:2605.13716, 2025): five diagnostic dimensions (Utility, Redundancy, Compatibility, Failure-Risk, Validation-Gap) all map to existing Odysseus fields

## Files to Change

- `services/memory/skills.py` — `_compute_idf()`, `_bm25_score()`, `_health_score()`, IDF cache, hybrid scoring in `get_relevant_skills()`, `health_score` in `to_dict()`
- `static/js/skills.js` — health score badge rendering
- `tests/test_skill_retrieval_bm25.py` — 6 new tests (NEW FILE)

## Labels

`enhancement`, `skills`, `brain`
title: feat(skills): BM25 hybrid retrieval scoring + composite skill health score

body:
## Problem

Four bugs in the `auto_approve_skills` preference handling break the autonomous skill cultivation pipeline.

### Bug 1 — `skill_extractor.py`: extraction has unnecessary pref dependency (`~line 274`)

The extractor checks `auto_approve_skills` to decide draft vs published status at extraction time. This is semantically wrong. Extraction should always produce draft skills — the audit pipeline is the quality gate, not the extractor. Currently, the check also defaults to `False`, making the code correct by accident, but the logic conflates two distinct concepts.

### Bug 2 — `agent_loop.py:1242`: injection gate blocks all drafts including teacher-escalation

`agent_loop.py:1242` defaults `auto_approve_skills` to `False`, which causes `_skill_min_conf = 2.0` always. No draft can have confidence ≥ 2.0. Teacher-escalation drafts with confidence=0.9 are blocked.

The `skills.py:657-662` design comment explicitly documents that teacher drafts should inject "without a manual publish click" — so the student agent can retry a failed task on the next turn. This is the SkillWeaver strong→weak model skill transfer pattern (arxiv:2504.07079, +54.3% task success). The current code breaks this entirely.

### Bug 3 — `skills_routes.py:504`: audit can never promote skills

`skills_routes.py:504` defaults `auto_approve_skills` to `False`. The `_audit_finalize_status()` function receives `auto_publish=False` and never publishes even on verdict=pass, confidence=0.95. The 6-stage audit pipeline runs but cannot act on its results.

Per SkillsBench (arxiv:2602.12670), self-generated skills without curation provide zero benefit — and the audit IS the curation. An informational-only audit with no promotion path produces the same result as no audit.

### Bug 4 — `tool_implementations.py:241`: agent-added skills auto-publish (missed)

`tool_implementations.py:241` defaults `auto_approve_skills` to `True` in the `manage_skills add` fallback. Agent-added skills publish immediately without going through the audit pipeline — the opposite of what the extractor does.

### Pre-existing gap — `teacher_escalation.py`: suggested confidence 0.8 < injection floor 0.85

The teacher prompt template suggests `"confidence": 0.8` (lines ~195 and ~293). The injection floor is `0.85`. Teacher-written drafts with LLM-generated confidence ≤ 0.84 fail the injection gate, silently breaking the teacher→student transfer path.

## Fix

1. **`skill_extractor.py`**: Remove `auto_approve_skills` pref check entirely. Always save as draft. Extraction is always draft; audit handles promotion.

2. **`agent_loop.py`**: Restore default `True`. Replace `min_conf=2.0` hack with a source-aware pre-filter that includes `published` skills and `source=teacher-escalation` drafts when `auto_approve_skills=False`. When `True` (default), all skills pass to `get_relevant_skills()` at the normal confidence floor.

3. **`skills_routes.py`**: Restore default `True`. The audit IS the quality gate; it must be able to promote passing skills.

4. **`tool_implementations.py`**: Remove pref check from `manage_skills add` fallback. Always draft. Agent-added skills go through the same audit pipeline.

5. **`teacher_escalation.py`** (~195, ~293): Change suggested confidence `0.8` → `0.9` (two locations). Ensures teacher-written drafts reliably clear the 0.85 injection floor.

## Research Basis

- **SkillsBench** (arxiv:2602.12670, 2025): curated skills raise pass rate +16 pp; uncurated provide zero benefit. The audit must be able to promote.
- **SkillWeaver** (arxiv:2504.07079, 2025): strong→weak model skill transfer requires immediate injection availability (+54.3% task success on WebArena).

## Files Changed

- `services/memory/skill_extractor.py` — remove pref check
- `src/agent_loop.py` — restore default; source-aware pre-filter
- `routes/skills_routes.py` — restore default
- `src/tool_implementations.py` — remove pref check from add fallback
- `src/teacher_escalation.py` — confidence 0.8→0.9 (two locations)
- `services/memory/skills.py` — update design comment to reflect both modes
- `tests/test_skill_extraction_gate.py` — update 3 tests for corrected defaults
- `tests/test_skill_lifecycle_correctness.py` — 10 new tests (NEW FILE)

## Type of Change

Bug fix (correctness)
title: fix(skills): auto_approve_skills semantics broken — extraction always draft, audit defaults to trust

body:
## Problem

Three strings in \`src/agent_loop.py\` instruct the agent to consult the skill registry before every task and to treat extracted skills as proven, authoritative procedures. Together they produce a mandatory pre-task consultation loop that consumes agent rounds on overhead before any user work begins.

**String 1 — \`manage_skills\` tool description (line ~417):**
> "Use this **BEFORE doing domain work** — there may already be a procedure (published or draft) that prescribes the correct steps. Drafts written by the teacher loop are **authoritative guidance** even though they're not yet published."

This instructs the agent to call \`manage_skills list\` before starting any task. For tasks with a non-empty skill index, the agent then calls \`manage_skills view\` for each seemingly relevant skill — consuming 2–3 rounds before the actual work begins.

**String 2 — matched-skills injection header (lines ~1274-1279):**
> "Each is a **procedure proven to work**. **Follow them step by step.**"

Skills are LLM extractions from a 12-message context window — they are approximations, not verified facts. "Proven to work" is a false claim. "Follow them step by step" causes unconditional execution even when the skill mismatches the current task.

**String 3 — skill index block header (lines ~1447-1453):**
> "Procedures the assistant should **consult before doing domain work**. [...] **treat them as authoritative guidance**"

Same pattern: mandatory pre-task gate + unconditional deference.

**Observed behavior:** The agent calls \`manage_skills\` at the start of nearly every session that has skills present. On tasks with a large skill index, this is 2–4 extra rounds before user work starts.

## Proposed fix

**\`src/agent_loop.py\` — 3 string replacements:**

**Change 1 (line 417):** Replace "BEFORE doing domain work" and "authoritative guidance" with conditional language — check the registry when the domain looks familiar, treat published skills as reviewed and drafts as candidates.

**Change 2 (lines 1274-1279):** Replace "proven to work. Follow them step by step." with "candidate procedures. Evaluate fit — apply if relevant, use own judgment if not."

**Change 3 (lines 1447-1453):** Replace "consult before doing domain work" and "treat them as authoritative guidance" with "reference procedures for this session. When a task closely matches, apply; evaluate drafts before following."

## Tests

New file \`tests/test_agent_skill_prompt_language.py\` — 6 static source-text assertions:
1. "BEFORE doing domain work" not in agent_loop.py source
2. "authoritative guidance" not in manage_skills tool description block
3. "proven to work" not in agent_loop.py source
4. "Follow them step by step" not in agent_loop.py source
5. "consult before doing domain work" not in agent_loop.py source
6. "treat them as authoritative" not in agent_loop.py source

## Upstream relevance

ROADMAP lists "Agent prompt/context bloat" as high priority. Removing the mandatory pre-task consultation loop directly reduces per-request token overhead and agent round consumption. References upstream issue #2750 "Agent prompt token bloat: measure, slim, and modularize".

**Branch:** \`fix/skill-agent-prompt-language\` (from \`upstream-mirror\`)
**Upstream target:** \`pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus\` dev branch

body:
## Problem

The skill auto-extraction system has three compounding defects that cause low-quality skills to accumulate and be injected into agent context without user review:

**1. Extraction gate fires on trivially short sessions**

The gate in \`routes/chat_helpers.py\` triggers when \`agent_rounds >= 2 OR agent_tool_calls >= 2\`. Nearly every agent interaction qualifies — a task that reads a file and writes it back (2 tool calls, 1 round) is enough. The corresponding gate in \`services/memory/skill_extractor.py\` uses the same OR logic. This is not selective enough to identify genuinely reusable procedures.

**2. Confidence threshold mismatch creates zombie skills**

\`MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.6\` in \`skill_extractor.py\` saves skills to disk. The injection gate in \`agent_loop.py\` defaults to \`skill_min_confidence = 0.85\`. Skills with confidence 0.60–0.84 are saved but never surfaced to the agent — they accumulate as dead weight in \`data/skills/\`.

**3. \`auto_approve_skills\` defaults to \`True\`**

Extracted skills are auto-published without user review. A skill extracted from a failed or one-off session immediately becomes part of the agent's injected context on the next turn. There is no gate for human judgment before a skill goes live.

**Observed result:** Low-quality skills (libvirt XML config procedures, etc.) have already appeared in \`data/skills/\` from routine agent tasks. Each extracted skill adds to the skill index, increasing prompt token usage on every subsequent agent request.

## Proposed fix

**\`services/memory/skill_extractor.py\`:**
- Raise \`MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.6\` → \`0.85\` (align with injection floor; stop saving skills that will never be injected)
- Change gate condition: \`if round_count < 2 and tool_count < 2\` → \`if round_count < 2 or tool_count < 3\` (require rounds ≥ 2 AND tools ≥ 3 — both conditions, not either)
- Change \`auto_approve_skills\` pref default: \`True\` → \`False\` (skills land as drafts; user publishes from Brain > Skills)

**\`routes/chat_helpers.py\`:**
- Change outer gate: \`(agent_rounds >= 2 or agent_tool_calls >= 2)\` → \`(agent_rounds >= 2 and agent_tool_calls >= 3)\` (match the new AND logic)

## Tests

New file \`tests/test_skill_extraction_gate.py\` — 5 async unit tests using monkeypatch (pattern: \`test_skill_extractor_stray_brace.py\`):
1. rounds=1, tools=2 → skipped (below new combined threshold)
2. rounds=2, tools=2 → skipped (tools below 3)
3. rounds=2, tools=3 → proceeds to LLM call
4. confidence=0.84 → dropped (below new MIN_CONFIDENCE)
5. auto_approve default=False → skill status is "draft" not "published"

## Upstream relevance

ROADMAP lists "Agent prompt/context bloat" as high priority. This fix reduces the volume of skills injected into context by raising the bar for what qualifies as extractable. Relates to #4520 (junk name rejection) and upstream issue #4466 (skill curation).

**Branch:** \`fix/skill-extraction-threshold\` (from \`upstream-mirror\`)
**Upstream target:** \`pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus\` dev branch

## Problem

Three GC issues in chatHistory.js and chat.js discovered during a full GC stack audit:

**1. Missing idle GC signal after `_evictLive` and `_pruneBottom`**

`_pruneTop` already yields with `requestIdleCallback(() => {}, { timeout: 3000 })` after detaching subtrees, giving V8/Oilpan the idle hint it needs to schedule incremental collection. `_evictLive` and `_pruneBottom` both create detached subtrees but never yield — the hint is missing, leaving Oilpan without a collection trigger after the two most common prune operations.

**2. Timer and renderer teardown gap in `_pruneTop` and `_pruneBottom`**

`_evictLive` correctly clears `_waveInterval`, `_elapsedTicker`, and `_streamRenderer` on every removed element and its descendants before `.remove()`. `_pruneTop` and `_pruneBottom` only call `hljsDeferForgetNode` — the interval and renderer cleanup is skipped, leaving live timers running on detached nodes and `_streamRenderer` references preventing StreamRenderer collection.

**3. Stale background stream Map entries accumulate across session switches**

`_purgeStaleBackgroundStreams()` sweeps `_backgroundStreams` for completed/error entries. It was called only in `handleChatSubmit`. On session switches (via `checkBackgroundStream`), completed entries persisted in the Map until the next chat submit.

## Fix

- Add `requestIdleCallback(() => {}, { timeout: 3000 })` at the end of `_evictLive` and inside `_pruneBottom`'s `if (removed > 0)` block.
- Add the `_waveInterval` / `_elapsedTicker` / `_streamRenderer` teardown loop (mirroring `_evictLive`) to all four removal sites in `_pruneTop` and `_pruneBottom` (main loop + boundary cleanup in each).
- Call `_purgeStaleBackgroundStreams()` at the top of `checkBackgroundStream`.

## Files

- `static/js/chatHistory.js` — rIC signal + teardown gap
- `static/js/chat.js` — purge on session switch

## Tests

5 new static-analysis tests:
- `tests/test_chat_history_js.py` (+4): `test_evict_live_yields_to_idle`, `test_prune_bottom_yields_to_idle`, `test_prune_top_clears_intervals_before_remove`, `test_prune_bottom_clears_intervals_before_remove`
- `tests/test_chat_gc_hint_js.py` (+1): `test_check_background_stream_purges_stale`

Note: `chatHistory.js` is a fork addition (DOM virtualization); these fixes will ship upstream with the DOM virtualization PR.

body:
## Problem

Six targeted GC/memory improvements identified through a full audit of the GC stack (chat.js, chatHistory.js, markdown.js, qt_wrapper.py):

1. **Missing idle GC signal after `_evictLive` and `_pruneBottom`** — `_pruneTop` already yields with `requestIdleCallback(() => {}, { timeout: 3000 })` after detaching subtrees. `_evictLive` and `_pruneBottom` create detached subtrees but never yield, leaving V8/Oilpan without the idle hint needed to trigger incremental collection.

2. **Missing timer/renderer teardown in `_pruneTop` and `_pruneBottom`** — `_evictLive` correctly clears `_waveInterval`, `_elapsedTicker`, and `_streamRenderer` on every removed element and its descendants before `.remove()`. `_pruneTop` and `_pruneBottom` only call `hljsDeferForgetNode`, leaving live timers on detached nodes.

3. **`squashOutsideCode` allocates on every render frame** — called at ~30 fps during streaming. For the common case (plain text, no code blocks) it allocates a `split` array and `join` string that are immediately discarded. A `str.includes('```')` guard short-circuits the whole allocation.

4. **7 direct `window.hljs.highlightElement` calls bypass `deferHighlightAll`** — `deferHighlightAll` (already imported) uses IntersectionObserver to highlight only visible code blocks. 4 of the 7 sites highlight off-screen blocks synchronously, blocking the main thread on large responses.

5. **`_purgeStaleBackgroundStreams` called only on chat submit** — completed/error background stream Map entries persist across session switches and accumulate until the next submit. `checkBackgroundStream` is invoked on every session switch and is the correct place to run the purge.

## Fix

- **A:** Add `requestIdleCallback(() => {}, { timeout: 3000 })` at the end of `_evictLive` and inside the `if (removed > 0)` block of `_pruneBottom`.
- **A+:** Add full timer/renderer teardown (`_waveInterval`, `_elapsedTicker`, `_streamRenderer` + descendant walk) before each `.remove()` call in `_pruneTop` and `_pruneBottom`, mirroring the pattern already in `_evictLive`.
- **B:** Add `if (!str.includes('```')) { return str.replace(...); }` fast path to `squashOutsideCode` in `markdown.js`.
- **C:** Replace 7 `window.hljs.highlightElement` forEach loops in `chat.js` with `deferHighlightAll(container)`.
- **F:** Call `_purgeStaleBackgroundStreams()` at the top of `checkBackgroundStream` in `chat.js`.

## Files

- `static/js/chatHistory.js` — Changes A, A+
- `static/js/markdown.js` — Change B
- `static/js/chat.js` — Changes C, F

15 new static-analysis tests across 4 files:

- `tests/test_markdown_squash_js.py` (new, 3)
- `tests/test_chat_hljs_defer_js.py` (new, 3)

body:
## Problem

Two distinct performance problems make typing feel laggy with occasional 1-second freezes:

**1-second lockups:** `Memory.forciblyPurgeJavaScriptMemory` via CDP calls `V8::LowMemoryNotification()` synchronously in the renderer, blocking the JS event loop for 100 ms–1 s+ depending on heap size. This fires:
- From the PSI monitor every 5 s when `avg10 > 5 %` — no cooldown, so it can fire repeatedly during a long typing session
- From `changeEvent(WindowDeactivate)` on every focus shift (notifications, alt-tab, clicking into a dialog) on KDE/Wayland

**General jankiness:** `autoResize` (ui.js) reads `getComputedStyle`, `textarea.offsetWidth`, and `clone.scrollHeight` on every keystroke — 2 forced layout reflows per character. At 8 chars/sec this is 16 forced layout reflows/sec in QtWebEngine, which is slower than a desktop browser.

## Fix

**`static/js/ui.js` — autoResize:** Replace clone-based synchronous measurement with `requestAnimationFrame`-coalesced `height: 'auto'` + `scrollHeight`. N keystrokes per 16 ms frame → 1 layout reflow (vs. 2 per keystroke before). Drop clone entirely.

**`qt_wrapper.py` — async GC overhaul:**
- Remove `_cdp_purge_memory` (the synchronous stop-the-world variant)
- Replace all three trigger sites with `gc({ type: 'major', execution: 'async' })` via `page.runJavaScript()` — already enabled by `--expose-gc`; non-blocking, incremental
- Add 500 ms debounce on focus-loss (skips transient focus shifts)
- Add 30 s cooldown on PSI purge (prevents repeated GC bursts under sustained pressure)
- Node-threshold trigger calls `runJavaScript` directly (already on Qt main thread)
- PSI monitor (background thread) uses a 250 ms drain timer on the main thread — correct cross-thread dispatch without needing `QTimer.singleShot` from a non-Qt thread

## Files

- `static/js/ui.js` — `autoResize` rewrite
- `qt_wrapper.py` — remove `_cdp_purge_memory`, add `_request_async_gc`, update PSI/focus-loss/node-threshold

## Tests

- New `tests/test_ui_auto_resize_js.py` (5 tests)
- Updated `tests/test_qt_cdp_listener_audit.py` (−7 old, +9 new = 43 total)

body:
## Problem

`QtWebEngineProcess` (and any embedded Chromium) accumulates Oilpan/Blink detached DOM
nodes during agent sessions with rapid tool-call rounds, even with the 2.5s post-response
`gc()` call in place.

### Root cause: `_gcPending` lockout in rapid agent loops

The 5000ms lockout window means that when 4 rapid tool responses complete in succession,
only the first gets a GC cycle. Responses 2–4 accumulate Oilpan garbage with no
collection:

```
T=0s   Response 1 finishes → gc() dispatched → _gcPending = true
T=2s   Response 2 finishes → gc() BLOCKED (_gcPending)
T=4s   Response 3 finishes → gc() BLOCKED
T=6s   Response 4 finishes → gc() BLOCKED
T=5s   _gcPending = false  ← no catch-up fires; 3 responses' garbage stranded
```

There is no mechanism to detect that GC was blocked or to collect the missed cycles.

### Secondary: element-node in-place patch uses `innerHTML` unnecessarily

`streamingRenderer.js` in-place patch uses `_tailNodes[i].innerHTML = newNodes[i].innerHTML`
for element-node updates, which destroys and recreates child nodes even when both old and
new have a single text child. The simpler `firstChild.data =` assignment suffices and
avoids one detach+create cycle per token for plain-text elements.

## Solution

**A: Missed-GC catch-up flag** — reduce lockout 5000ms → 3000ms; add `_gcMissed` flag;
when GC completes and `_gcMissed` is true, immediately dispatch one catch-up GC cycle and
log `[GC] catch-up dispatched`. A run of N rapid responses gets at most 2 GC cycles
(primary + catch-up) rather than 1.

**B: Element-node text-data patch** — for element nodes where both live and new have a
single text-node child, use `firstChild.data =` instead of `innerHTML =`. Adds `_rtSaved`
counter logged in `finalize()` alongside the existing `_rtCalls`/`_rtFast` metrics.

## Context

This primarily affects embedded Chromium (QtWebEngine, Electron) where OS memory pressure
signals are not wired to Oilpan's coordinator, so Oilpan never spontaneously runs a major
collection. `gc({ type: 'major', execution: 'async' })` via `--expose-gc` is the only
reliable mechanism — making it fire reliably between agent rounds is critical for
long-running sessions.

`[GC] blocked — catch-up queued` and `[GC] catch-up dispatched` log lines route through
`javaScriptConsoleMessage` into `wrapper_system.log` for diagnostic visibility.

body:
## Problem

`streamingRenderer.js renderTail()` creates a full holder div on every SSE token:

```javascript
const holder = document.createElement('div');
holder.innerHTML = render(tailText);       // full markdown parse → full DOM subtree
const newNodes = Array.from(holder.childNodes);
```

Even when the fast path succeeds (same node count, same node types) and the holder nodes are patched in-place rather than inserted, the holder and its full parsed DOM subtree are still created and immediately become Oilpan garbage. At 30fps this is ~300 complete DOM trees created and discarded per 10-second streaming response.

## Fix

Add a text-only append fast path that fires **before** the holder is created. For the common case — plain prose streaming where new tokens contain no markdown structural characters — detect that the tail is growing by plain text and update the deepest text node directly. No holder needed.

Tracking: `_lastTailText` records the text from the last successful call. If new tail starts with that text and the new suffix has no structural characters, walk to the deepest text node in the last tail node and append the suffix to its `.data`.

## What this covers
- Plain prose streaming (dominant token type in conversational agent responses)
- Falls through correctly on any structural character (bold, italic, code fence, heading, newline)

## Estimated impact
60–80% fewer holder div allocations for prose-heavy agent responses. The `[streamRenderer] renderTail calls=N fast=M (P%)` log line will show an increase in the fast-path percentage.

body:
## Problem

When a thinking-block agent response finishes, `chat.js` currently does:

```javascript
if (_liveReplyEl && _finalReply) {
  var _replyHtml = markdownModule.mdToHtml(markdownModule.squashOutsideCode(_finalReply));
  _liveReplyEl.innerHTML = _replyHtml;
```

`_liveReplyEl._streamRenderer` was built up incrementally during streaming and already holds the correct content. The `innerHTML = mdToHtml()` call creates an entirely new DOM tree and discards the streamed one — one complete response-worth of detached Oilpan nodes per agent exchange.

## Fix

When `_liveReplyEl._streamRenderer` exists, call `update(_finalReply)` to sync to the final post-processed text, then `finalize()` to freeze in place. Fall back to the existing `innerHTML` path only when the renderer is absent.

## Impact

Eliminates the largest single-event Oilpan deposition per agent response — one full response-worth of DOM nodes freed per exchange rather than discarded as detached garbage.

Related to the OOM investigation in the fork.

## Problem

We have post-response async GC firing via `gc({ type: 'major', execution: 'async' })` in chat.js, and CDP node-count polling via qt_wrapper.py. But we have no way to correlate:
- Whether `gc()` actually fires (vs being skipped silently)
- How many `renderTail()` calls per response hit the fast-path in-place patch vs the full clear+rebuild

Without this data, we can't quantify Source 1 (renderTail shadow DOM) or validate that GC is working.

## Changes

**chat.js** — add `console.log('[GC] major async dispatched')` before the `gc()` call in the post-response setTimeout. This line appears in `wrapper_system.log` (JS console output is captured via `javaScriptConsoleMessage`) and can be correlated against `[CDP] nodes=N` lines.

**streamingRenderer.js** — add `_rtCalls` / `_rtFast` counters inside the `createStreamRenderer` closure. Increment `_rtCalls` at the top of `renderTail()`, increment `_rtFast` on the fast-path return. Log both in `finalize()`:
```
[streamRenderer] renderTail calls=247 fast=231 (94%)
```

## Why this matters

The fast-path ratio directly determines whether the render-free optimization (Opportunity 4 in memory-explosion-research.md) is worth the implementation cost. If 95%+ are fast-path, the holder-div allocation is the dominant ongoing Oilpan pressure. If only 50% are fast-path, structure changes are also a significant source.

## Classification

Upstream-candidate. Pure observability addition — no behavioral change.
