body:
## Context

`fix/gguf-quality-scored` (filed after `feat/aria2c-downloader`) adds a quality-scored GGUF source discovery endpoint (`/api/cookbook/resolve-gguf`) powered by `HfUrlResolver.find_gguf_sources()`. It fires as a fallback when a llama.cpp download has no pre-configured GGUF source.

Two gaps remain:

---

## Gap 1 — imatrix quants are invisible to the hwfit tier selector

`services/hwfit/models.py` line 5:

```python
QUANT_HIERARCHY = ["Q8_0", "Q6_K", "Q5_K_M", "Q4_K_M", "Q3_K_M", "Q2_K"]
```

These are all standard K-quants. Imatrix variants (`IQ4_XS`, `IQ4_NL`, `IQ3_M`, `IQ3_S`, `IQ2_M`) are not in the hierarchy at all.

Effect: when the hwfit recommends Q4_K_M for a user's hardware, the download targets a Q4_K_M file. It never discovers `bartowski/Model-GGUF` or `mradermacher/Model-GGUF-imatrix`, which produce `IQ4_XS` files that have measurably better perplexity at the same or smaller file size.

`QUANT_BPP` also needs IQ-family BPP values so the memory estimator can size them correctly.

**Fix:** expand `QUANT_HIERARCHY` to include imatrix variants alongside or above their K-quant equivalents. Preliminary order by quality/size tradeoff:

```python
QUANT_HIERARCHY = [
    "Q8_0",
    "Q6_K",
    "Q5_K_M", "Q5_K_S",
    "IQ4_XS", "IQ4_NL", "Q4_K_M", "Q4_K_S",
    "IQ3_M", "Q3_K_L", "Q3_K_M", "Q3_K_S",
    "IQ2_M", "Q2_K",
]
```

---

## Gap 2 — resolver runs on llama.cpp only, and only when config is missing

The resolver currently fires only when:
- Backend is `llamacpp`
- AND the model has no pre-configured GGUF source

It should run for **all llama.cpp downloads** and pick the highest-quality available repo rather than always downloading from the base model repo.

Additionally, vLLM and SGLang downloads always get the base BF16/FP16 repo. They never check for:

- **FP8** quantized repos (e.g. `neuralmagic/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-FP8`) — near-zero quality loss, 2× throughput on H100/H200/A100 newer silicon
- **AWQ-4bit** repos (e.g. `hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4`) — 4× memory reduction with good quality, compatible with any CUDA GPU
- **compressed-tensors** / LLMCompressor repos — the emerging vLLM-native format

The hwfit already has `QUANT_QUALITY_PENALTY`, `QUANT_SPEED_MULT`, and `QUANT_BPP` for these formats and knows FP8 > AWQ-8bit > AWQ-4bit for quality. The scoring infrastructure exists; the discovery does not.

**Fix:** extend `HfUrlResolver` with a `find_vllm_sources(base_repo_id, preferred_formats)` method that searches for optimized repos by format, filtered to what the serving hardware supports:

- H100 / H200 / A100 (compute capability ≥ 8.9) → prefer FP8, then AWQ-4bit
- RTX 30/40 series (compute capability ≥ 8.0) → prefer AWQ-4bit, then GPTQ-Int4
- Older / CPU → stay on base BF16 (quantized serving not supported)

---

## Scope

- `services/hwfit/models.py` — add imatrix variants to `QUANT_HIERARCHY` and `QUANT_BPP`
- `tooling/hf_url_resolver.py` — add `find_vllm_sources()` alongside `find_gguf_sources()`
- `routes/cookbook_routes.py` — add `/api/cookbook/resolve-vllm` endpoint, wire resolver into all llama.cpp download paths (not just the missing-config fallback)
- `static/js/cookbookDownload.js` — call the discovery endpoints for all backend downloads, not just the fallback case
- Tests: unit tests for `find_vllm_sources()` scoring; static checks for the expanded hierarchy

## Dependencies

Depends on `feat/aria2c-downloader` (introduces `HfUrlResolver` base class) and `fix/gguf-quality-scored` (establishes the GGUF discovery pattern and scoring machinery). Both must be upstream-merged before this can land.

## Out of scope

- Changing what the user asked to download (quant preference is still honoured; this is about *which repo* supplies the file, not *which quant tier*)
- After-the-fact scanning of already-downloaded models (separate feature if desired)
- Q8_0 tier improvements: Q8_0 is effectively the ceiling for GGUF; there is no IQ8 format and imatrix calibration provides negligible benefit at 8 bits
title: feat(resolver): expand quality-scored source discovery to all backends and imatrix quant tiers

body:
## Summary

When Gemma 4 is self-hosted through Ollama, llama-cpp-python, or mlx-lm and the serving layer does not properly handle the Gemma 4 chat template, raw model-output tokens leak to the client unformatted. These tokens are neither executed as tool calls nor stripped, and appear as literal text in the chat.

**This does not affect Google's hosted Gemini/Gemma API**, which translates the raw tokens server-side into the `<tool_code>func()</tool_code>` Python-call format (addressed separately in issue #35). It also does not affect the Google OpenAI-compat endpoint for the same reason.

This is strictly a self-hosted path problem: Odysseus → Ollama/llama-cpp-python/mlx-lm → Gemma 4 model.

## Format

Gemma 4's raw tool-call token sequence (before chat template processing):

```
<|tool_call>call:fn_name{key:<|"|>value<|"|>}<tool_call|>
```

Key characteristics:
- **Asymmetric special tokens:** `<|tool_call>` opens, `<tool_call|>` closes (note the `|` on opposite sides)
- **`call:` prefix** before the function name
- **Custom string encoding:** string values are wrapped in `<|"|>...<|"|>` pseudo-tokens, not standard JSON quotes
- **Not JSON-parseable as-is** — requires custom tokenization before the argument object can be decoded

Example (tool call with one string arg):
```
<|tool_call>call:bash{command:<|"|>gh repo list<|"|>}<tool_call|>
```

## Root cause

The serving layers (Ollama, llama-cpp-python, mlx-lm) each maintain their own chat template implementations. If a layer's Gemma 4 template was added before the tool-call format was documented, or has not been updated, it passes through the raw tokens rather than translating to an OpenAI-compat `tool_calls` response field.

The correct long-term fix is in the serving layers. This issue tracks an Odysseus-side parser as a fallback for users who encounter this before the serving layers fully converge.

## Scope (Odysseus-side)

- Add `_GEMMA4_TOOL_CALL_RE` to `src/tool_parsing.py` matching the `<|tool_call>call:fn{...}<tool_call|>` pattern
- Add `_parse_gemma4_tool_call()` that tokenizes the argument object (handles `<|"|>` string delimiters) and routes through `function_call_to_tool_block`
- Update `strip_tool_blocks` to remove unmatched or unparseable `<|tool_call>` tokens so they never reach the user

## Priority

**Low** — the local self-hosted path for 560B Gemma 4 is uncommon, and serving layer fixes are likely incoming. Revisit if Ollama's Gemma 4 template is confirmed broken with tool calls.

## References

- Google AI blog: Gemma 4 model card and tool-call spec (raw format)
- [mlx-lm](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm) — tracks chat template accuracy per model family
- [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp) — jinja template used for Gemma 4 serving
title: feat(tool_parsing): parse Gemma 4 raw tool-call format from local serving layers

body:
## Summary

Odysseus routes Google Gemini/Gemma traffic through Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint
(\`generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/\`). This is the right approach —
the compat endpoint is well-maintained and covers the core use cases — but the current
implementation has three known quirks handled with inline patches buried inside the
streaming accumulator, no Google-specific payload builder, and no test coverage.

This issue tracks a comprehensive hardening pass: catalogue every known quirk, isolate
all Google-specific logic into named helpers, and add tests for the untested behaviors.
The \`toolCalls\` camelCase fix is tracked separately in #39 and should land first.

---

## Known quirks — current state

### 1. `toolCalls` camelCase — tracked in #39

Google's compat endpoint sends \`toolCalls\` (camelCase) in delta chunks instead of
\`tool_calls\` (snake_case). Fix and tests are on \`fix/google-compat-toolcalls\` (#39).
That branch should be filed before this one.

### 2. Missing `index` on parallel tool calls (inline patch, no test)

Google sends each tool call complete in a single delta with \`index: null\`. Without the
fix, all parallel calls collide into slot 0 — later calls overwrite the first's name
and corrupt its arguments by concatenation, so only one malformed call survives and the
follow-up request 400s.

Current fix (lines ~2200–2220 of \`llm_core.py\`): allocates a fresh accumulator slot
when \`func.get("name")\` is present and \`index\` is None. Correct, but inline and untested.

### 3. `thought_signature` round-trip (inline patch, no test)

Gemini 3 returns an opaque \`thought_signature\` in \`extra_content\` on the function-call
delta. It must be echoed back on the assistant \`tool_call\` in the follow-up turn or the
request 400s with "Function call is missing a thought_signature."

Current fix (lines ~2224–2230): preserves \`extra_content\` verbatim in \`_tc_acc\`. No test.
No validation that the round-trip actually happens in \`_append_tool_results\`.

### 4. `content=None` on tool-calls-only assistant messages (sanitizer, no test)

Gemini (and Ollama) reject a \`tool_calls\` assistant message that also has \`content: ""\`
or \`content: null\`. The sanitizer at line ~1097 re-adds explicit \`content=None\` for
tool-calls-only assistant messages. Correct, but the comment calls out Gemini by name
with no test confirming the behavior.

---

## What this issue adds

### A. `_is_google_compat(url)` helper

Replace the bare \`_host_match(url, "googleapis.com")\` in \`_detect_provider\` with a
named function so the detection logic can be tested and reused without duplicating the
host check.

### B. `_build_google_compat_payload()` function

Google currently falls through to the generic \`else\` branch in \`stream_llm\` — it gets
a raw OpenAI payload with no specialisation. A \`_build_google_compat_payload()\` function
(parallel to \`_build_anthropic_payload\` and \`_build_ollama_payload\`) makes the
Google-specific concerns explicit and removes them from the generic path. Minimum scope:

- Validates and preserves \`thought_signature\` on tool call messages before sending
- Documents why temperature and \`max_tokens\` pass through as-is (compat translates them)
- Centralises the \`content=None\` tool-calls-only guard so the sanitizer comment can be removed

### C. Extract Google streaming helpers

The two inline quirk patches for index=None and thought_signature are separated into
named functions called from the streaming loop:

- \`_google_assign_tc_index(tc, func, acc, last_idx)\` — slot allocation for index=None
- \`thought_signature\` preservation stays in the accumulator but with a clear
  Google-attributed comment block, not buried in generic tool-call logic

### D. Tests — `tests/test_google_compat.py`

One test per untested quirk (quirk 1 is covered by #39):

1. Parallel tool calls with \`index=None\` land in distinct slots (two calls, verify two entries)
2. \`thought_signature\` is preserved in \`_tc_acc\` and survives the follow-up message build
3. Tool-calls-only assistant message has \`content=None\`, not \`content: ""\`

---

## Filing order

File #39 (\`fix/google-compat-toolcalls\`) before this one. This issue references the
camelCase fix as prior art and builds on it.

---

## Out of scope

- Google native \`generateContent\` API — the compat endpoint handles the core use case
  reliably after this hardening pass, and a native path would duplicate the entire
  request/response cycle for marginal gain
- Context caching, grounding, Imagen/Veo — compat-endpoint-only features; not in scope
  for this refactor

---

## Files

- \`src/llm_core.py\` — all changes
- \`tests/test_google_compat.py\` — new test file (3 tests; quirk 1 test is on #39)
title: refactor(llm_core): harden Google OpenAI-compat layer — payload builder, quirk isolation, test coverage

body:
## Summary

Google's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`) has multiple documented bugs affecting tool call handling for Gemini and Gemma models. This issue covers the bugs that directly affect Odysseus.

## Bug 1 — field name mismatch (camelCase) ← affects Odysseus, fix implemented

The endpoint returns `toolCalls` (camelCase) instead of `tool_calls` (snake_case). Odysseus's streaming accumulator in `llm_core.py` calls `delta.get("tool_calls")` which returns `None` when Google sends `toolCalls`. Native tool calls are silently dropped and the model falls back to text-based `<tool_code>` output.

**Fix:** check both `delta.get("tool_calls")` and `delta.get("toolCalls")` in the streaming accumulator and in the delta-has-output guard used for usage tracking.

**Scope:** streaming path only (`llm_core.py`). Odysseus routes all LLM calls through SSE streaming so no non-streaming path is affected.

## Bug 2 — finish_reason wrong value ← does NOT affect Odysseus

The endpoint returns `finish_reason: "stop"` instead of `"tool_calls"` when a tool call is made. Odysseus never gates on `finish_reason` to detect tool calls (confirmed by code audit — the field appears only in a comment in `llm_core.py`). No fix needed here.

Documented for completeness: [Google AI Forum thread](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/the-finish-reason-is-stop-instead-of-tool_calls-in-openai-compatible-endpoint/112704)

## Bug 3 — parameterless functions rejected (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT) ← may affect Odysseus

Sending a function definition with an empty `parameters` object causes a 400 error. Workaround: omit the `parameters` key entirely rather than passing `{}`. Odysseus may hit this for tools that take no arguments (e.g. `get_workspace`, `list_models`). Not yet confirmed.

## Bug 4 — tool_call_id too long ← unclear impact

Google returns `tool_call_id` values that exceed the length Odysseus sends back in the tool result `tool_call_id` field. LiteLLM has a fix PR for this. Needs investigation.

## Bug 5 — streaming + tool_calls raises SDK errors ← unclear impact

Reported in openai-python issue #2806. May not affect Odysseus since it uses raw httpx streaming rather than the OpenAI SDK client.

## Files

`src/llm_core.py` only (Bug 1). Bugs 3–5 may require separate investigation and fixes.

## References

- [Two tool calling bugs in OpenAI compatibility beta — Google AI Forum](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/two-tool-calling-bugs-i-found-in-openai-compatibility-beta/58174)
- [finish_reason is 'stop' instead of 'tool_calls' — Google AI Forum](https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/the-finish-reason-is-stop-instead-of-tool_calls-in-openai-compatible-endpoint/112704)
- [Gemini 3 flash streaming tool call error — openai-python #2806](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/issues/2806)

comments.body:
Closing — the premise is incorrect. Direct testing against Google's OpenAI-compat endpoint (generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/) confirms the streaming delta uses snake_case `tool_calls` as the OpenAI spec requires. No camelCase `toolCalls` key was observed. The fix is a no-op and the PR has no valid purpose.

Raw response captured from the endpoint shows `"tool_calls":[{...}]` in the delta chunk. The original citation (Google developer forum thread) covered a different deviation — a missing `index` field — not a camelCase key name.

A real bug IS present in the same response: `finish_reason: "stop"` is returned instead of `"tool_calls"` when a tool call is made. That will be tracked separately.

title: llm_core: Google OpenAI-compat endpoint sends toolCalls (camelCase) not tool_calls

body:
## Summary

LongCat (Meituan, `meituan/longcat-flash-chat`) is OpenAI-compatible but emits tool calls as custom XML in response text rather than in the standard `tool_calls` JSON field. Two format variants exist and both need to be handled.

## Model and API details

- **HuggingFace:** `meituan-longcat/LongCat-Flash-Chat` (560B MoE)
- **OpenRouter model ID:** `meituan/longcat-flash-chat`
- **Official API endpoint:** `https://api.longcat.chat/openai/v1/` (OpenAI-compat)
- An Anthropic-compat path also exists at `https://api.longcat.chat/anthropic/v1/` using the same API key
- Related variants: `LongCat-Flash-Thinking`, `LongCat-Flash-Lite`, `LongCat-Flash-Prover`, `LongCat-Next`

## Format variants

Variant A vs B appears to depend on the model version or invocation path — both are documented and both are real.

**Variant A** (JSON inside tag, per HuggingFace model card):
```xml
<longcat_tool_call>
{"name": "function_name", "arguments": {"param": "value"}}
</longcat_tool_call>
```

**Variant B** (named arg tags, per vLLM/Vercel community — matches observed output):
```xml
<longcat_tool_call>
  readFile
  <longcat_arg_key>path</longcat_arg_key>
  <longcat_arg_value>./app/pages/index.vue</longcat_arg_value>
</longcat_tool_call>
```

In Variant B the function name appears as plain text before any arg pairs. Multiple parallel tool calls are emitted as consecutive `<longcat_tool_call>` blocks with no separator between them.

## Scope

- Add `"longcat"` to `_model_supports_tools` in `src/agent_loop.py` so schemas are sent and the model uses the structured channel where the API supports it (matching both `meituan/longcat-flash-chat` and bare `longcat-*` model strings)
- Add `_LONGCAT_TOOL_CALL_RE` pattern and `_parse_longcat_tool_call()` to `src/tool_parsing.py` handling both variants; routes through `function_call_to_tool_block` for the full tool set
- Update `strip_tool_blocks` to remove `<longcat_tool_call>` blocks regardless of parse success — they should never reach the user as raw XML

## References

- [meituan-longcat/LongCat-Flash-Chat on HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-Flash-Chat)
- [Parsing custom XML tool calls from LongCat Flash models — Vercel community](https://community.vercel.com/t/parsing-custom-xml-tool-calls-from-longcat-flash-models-in-vercel-ai-sdk/33601)
- vLLM maintains a dedicated parser for this format, confirming custom handling is required industry-wide
title: tool_parsing + agent: LongCat (Meituan) tool call support

body:
## Summary

LongCat models emit tool calls in a `<longcat_tool_call>` format with `<longcat_arg_key>` / `<longcat_arg_value>` pairs. None of the existing patterns in `tool_parsing.py` recognize this format — calls are neither executed nor stripped, leaking raw XML into the chat.

## Observed format

```
<longcat_tool_call>
<longcat_arg_key>file_path</longcat_arg_key>
<longcat_arg_value>data/integrations.json</longcat_arg_value>
</longcat_tool_call>
```

## Why existing patterns miss it

- `_TOOL_CODE_RE` / `_TOOL_CODE_PYCALL_RE` — wrong outer tag
- `_XML_TOOL_CALL_RE` — matches `<prefix:tool_call>` (colon separator) but not `<prefix_tool_call>` (underscore)
- `_XML_INVOKE_RE` — different tag structure entirely

## Investigation needed

The tool name is not visible in the snippet above — the full format needs to be captured to understand where the function name is encoded (attribute, first child tag, or inline text).

## Scope

`src/tool_parsing.py` — add a new pattern and parser for the LongCat format. Also ensure `strip_tool_blocks` removes unrecognised `<*_tool_call>` blocks so they never reach the user.

## Branch

## Summary

`parse_tool_blocks` handles `<tool_code>` in MiniMax-M2.5's `{tool => 'name', args => '...'}` format but not Python function-call syntax emitted by Google Gemma models:

```
<tool_code>
bash(command="gh repo list")
</tool_code>
```

Because `_TOOL_CODE_RE` requires a `{...}` wrapper, Gemma-style calls are neither executed nor stripped from the response — they leak as raw XML into the chat.

## Root cause

`_TOOL_CODE_RE` (line ~53 in `tool_parsing.py`):
```python
r"<tool_code>\s*\{([\s\S]*?)\}\s*</tool_code>"
```

Only matches the `{...}` form. Python-call syntax (`func(kwarg=val)`) is unrecognised by both the parser and the stripper.

## Expected behaviour

- `<tool_code>bash(command="gh repo list")</tool_code>` → executes as a `bash` tool call
- `<tool_code>get_workspace()</tool_code>` → executes as a `get_workspace` tool call
- Any `<tool_code>` block that cannot be parsed is still stripped from display output

## Proposed fix

1. Add `_TOOL_CODE_PYCALL_RE` regex matching the Python-call form
2. Add `_parse_tool_code_pycall()` using `ast.parse` (already imported) to extract function name + kwargs and route through `_TOOL_NAME_MAP` / `function_call_to_tool_block`
3. Hook into `parse_tool_blocks` after the existing MiniMax check
4. Replace `_TOOL_CODE_RE.sub` in `strip_tool_blocks` with a broad `_TOOL_CODE_ANY_RE` that strips all `<tool_code>` formats — consistent with the existing docstring: "that markup should never reach the user regardless of whether it converted to a tool call"

## Files

`src/tool_parsing.py` only — no agent loop or schema changes.
title: tool_parsing: <tool_code> blocks with Python function-call syntax are not parsed or stripped

body:
## Summary

A targeted CSS-only performance pass addressing five categories of rendering inefficiency in `static/style.css`. All changes benefit desktop, Qt wrapper (Linux/NVIDIA/Wayland), tablet, and phone equally. No visual changes for standard desktop users.

## 1 — `will-change` cleanup (3 removals)

`will-change` pre-allocates a GPU compositor layer indefinitely. It is only correct on elements that are **actively about to animate**. On always-visible or low-frequency elements it wastes GPU VRAM on all platforms — on phones and tablets this consumes shared system RAM.

Remove from:
- `.model-picker-wrap` — always in the DOM; permanent GPU layer for a small dropdown
- `.doc-line-number-content` — static text; was pre-allocating a GPU layer per line number row
- `#email-lib-modal .email-lib-fab` — 420ms expand transition works without permanent pre-promotion

## 2 — CSS `contain` on isolated containers (3 additions)

`contain` scopes style/layout recalculation to a component. Without it, a DOM change inside `.chat-history` (every new message) triggers a full-document style pass. On mobile processors with lower memory bandwidth, this is the largest source of avoidable recalculation work.

- `.sidebar` → `contain: content` — scopes hover/navigation recalculations
- `.chat-history` → `contain: content` — scopes per-message DOM appends
- `.modal-content` → `contain: layout style` — conservative (allows provider picker overflow)

## 3 — `prefers-reduced-motion` global catch-all

17 existing per-component blocks cover a small fraction of the 143 `@keyframes` definitions. Hundreds of animations have no reduced-motion handling. Adding a global `*, *::before, *::after` catch-all at end of file covers all remaining cases. Uses `0.01ms` not `0` to preserve `animationend`/`transitionend` JS event delivery.

On Android battery saver and iOS reduce-motion (commonly enabled on mid-range tablets and phones), this converts the full animation workload to near-zero with one OS setting.

## 4 — `touch-action: manipulation` on interactive elements

Without this, mobile browsers wait 300ms after a tap to check for double-tap-zoom. Adding `touch-action: manipulation` to `button`, `a`, `[role="button"]`, `.list-item`, and `.dropdown-item` removes this delay. Pan and pinch-zoom are preserved. WCAG-safe.

## 5 — `filter: brightness()` hover → `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` guard

`filter: brightness()` on `:hover` causes two problems:
1. Creates a GPU compositor layer on hover (desktop: brief compositor cost on every hover)
2. Gets permanently stuck on touch devices — touch fires a hover event that doesn't clear until the next tap, leaving buttons visually "stuck" in highlighted state

11 instances fixed using the `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` pattern (CSS-Tricks documented approach). Samsung false-positive devices excluded by the `pointer: fine` condition. `:active` states added outside the query for correct press feedback on touch.

## Platform notes

All five changes combine to make the app measurably faster on low-power devices. The reduced-motion and touch-action changes are the most impactful for phone users; CSS containment is most impactful on tablets with integrated graphics.
title: CSS render performance pass: will-change cleanup, CSS containment, reduced-motion global, touch-action, hover fix

body:
## Description

Intermittent black screen flicker occurs across multiple interactive areas:

- Sidebar item hover → 1–2 frame black flash
- Cookbook modal open → flash during open animation
- Downloads dropdown open → black screen sometimes lasting seconds  
- Settings/Providers dropdown open → black screen sometimes lasting seconds

On the Qt desktop wrapper (Linux/NVIDIA/Wayland) the stalls last seconds due to a separate GPU backend issue. But even on other platforms, the underlying CSS cause wastes GPU work.

## Root Cause

`backdrop-filter: blur()` is applied to several elements that have **opaque solid backgrounds** (`var(--panel)`). The blur has no visible effect — it samples the layer behind the element, but the element's background is fully opaque so the blurred content is never visible. However, each `backdrop-filter` declaration promotes the element to a GPU compositor layer. When that element changes state (hover, show, hide), the compositor must invalidate and re-render the filter.

Affected elements:

| Selector | Line | `backdrop-filter` value |
|----------|------|-------------------------|
| `.sidebar` | 399 | `blur(10px)` — always visible; every sidebar hover flickers |
| `.dropdown` | 5863 | `blur(12px)` — layer created/destroyed on every dropdown show |
| import notification banner | 3911 | `blur(12px)` |
| `#styled-confirm-overlay` | 5133 | `blur(4px)` |
| `#styled-prompt-overlay` | 5203 | `blur(4px)` |
| recording indicator | 6059 | `blur(10px)` |
| `.search-overlay` | 6149 | `blur(6px)` |
| recording indicator (dup) | 8317 | `blur(10px)` |
| `.popper-dropdown` | 12219 | `blur(12px)` |
| `.doc-suggestion-banner` | 12654 | `blur(12px)` |

Additionally, the `cookbook-modal-enter` keyframe animation uses `filter: saturate(0.85) → saturate(1.05) → none`. Transitioning `filter` from a value to `none` at animation end triggers a compositor layer teardown on the final frame, causing a flash on Cookbook open.

## Fix

Remove `backdrop-filter` from all the selectors above (all have opaque backgrounds; the blur is invisible and unused). Remove `filter: saturate()` from the `cookbook-modal-enter` keyframes — keep only `opacity` and `transform`, which animate via the GPU compositor without layer teardown.

These are CSS-only changes with no visual regression on any platform.

## Related

The Qt desktop wrapper (`linux_wrapper.py`, issue #14) has additional GPU flag misconfiguration that amplifies these CSS issues on Linux/NVIDIA/Wayland. That fix is being tracked under #14.
title: Black screen flicker on sidebar hover, dropdown open, and modal open — backdrop-filter on opaque interactive elements

## Problem

Odysseus has 1038 logging calls across 100+ files but they're all hardcoded to INFO level with no debug mode, no structured output, no request tracing, and no per-subsystem control. When debugging issues in production, there's no way to enable verbose logging for specific subsystems (chat, agent, tools, LLM calls) without restarting with a code change.

## Solution

A comprehensive logging system with two modes:

### Normal Mode (default)
- INFO level to console + rotating file handler
- Structured output: `2026-06-10T14:00:00 [INFO] odysseus.chat: message received session=abc123`
- Log file: `logs/odysseous.log` (rotating, 10MB, 5 backups)
- Access log: `logs/access.log` (HTTP requests/responses)

### Debug Mode (ODYSSEUS_DEBUG=1)
- DEBUG level to console + file
- Per-subsystem control: `ODYSSEUS_DEBUG=chat,agent,tools` enables debug only for those areas
- Request correlation: every log line includes session ID where available
- LLM call timing: model, tokens, duration logged at DEBUG level
- Tool execution timing: tool name, args summary, duration, success/failure
- Structured JSON output option: `ODYSSEUS_LOG_FORMAT=json`

### Implementation

- `src/logging_config.py` — centralized logging configuration (replaces inline setup in app.py)
- Named logger hierarchy: `odysseus`, `odysseus.chat`, `odysseus.agent`, `odysseus.tools`, `odysseus.llm`, `odysseus.security`
- `ODYSSEUS_DEBUG` env var — enables debug mode
- `ODYSSEUS_LOG_FORMAT` — `text` (default) or `json`
- `ODYSSEUS_LOG_FILE` — log file path (existing, preserved)
- Request middleware adds session ID to logging context

## Files

- `src/logging_config.py` — new: centralized config with debug mode, JSON format, rotation
- `app.py` — replace inline logging setup with `setup_logging()` call
- `src/constants.py` — add LOG_FORMAT constant, keep existing LOG_* constants
- `core/middleware.py` — add request context middleware (session ID in logs)

## Labels

`upstream-candidate`, `enhancement`
title: feat: comprehensive structured logging system with debug mode

## Problem

When downloading a model with the llamacpp backend and no `ggufSource` configured, the auto-discovery feature (`/api/cookbook/resolve-gguf`) searches HuggingFace for `"{model_name} GGUF"` and returns the top results by downloads. This often surfaces low-quality or irrelevant repos that:

- Have "GGUF" in the name but contain no actual GGUF files
- Are from unknown quantizers with few downloads
- Don't match recognized quantization formats (Q4_K_M, IQ4_XS, etc.)

Users see "No GGUF is configured" for models like `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` and `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct` because the discovery results don't contain usable quantization repos.

## Expected Behavior

The discovery should return repos that are actually GGUF quantizations, ranked by quality. Quality signals:

1. **Quantization format** in repo name (e.g., `Q4_K_M`, `IQ4_XS`, `F16`)
2. **Explicit GGUF naming** in repo name
3. **Model name match** (repo name contains the exact model name)
4. **Same-owner bonus** (repo owner matches the base model's owner)

## Proposed Fix

Enhance `HfUrlResolver.find_gguf_sources()` in `tooling/hf_url_resolver.py` to score and filter candidate repos by these quality signals, returning only repos that have at least one strong signal (quantization format or explicit GGUF naming).

## Files

- `tooling/hf_url_resolver.py` — `find_gguf_sources()` method

`upstream-candidate`, `enhancement`

`src/agent_tools/filesystem_tools.py` imports `_resolve_tool_path_in_workspace` from `src/tool_execution.py`, but that function was deleted by `0aba00f` (refactor: remove dead workspace-confinement plumbing). Three related scroll bugs in the DOM virtualization system (`chatHistory.js`):

**Bug 1 — Scroll-to-bottom button stops at current DOM bottom**
When Phase 3 has pruned newer history and a `_bSentinel` exists, the button's smooth-scroll loop targets `scrollHeight - clientHeight` of the *current* partial DOM. It settles there without ever draining the remaining `_loadNewer()` batches. The user is left at the top of the last rendered window, not the actual last message.

**Bug 2 — Session loads showing oldest rendered message, not newest**
On session switch, `scrollTop` lands at 0 instead of the bottom of the 50-message window. The single rAF in `load()` fires at the same paint as `scrollHistoryInstant()`, and neither corrects the position after the browser commits layout for the newly-visible container.

**Bug 3 — Scroll jump (and occasional black flicker) during streaming**
`_pruneTop()` removes nodes (reducing `scrollHeight`), then inserts a height-matched spacer. Between removal and insertion the browser clamps `scrollTop` downward. The spacer restores `scrollHeight` but `scrollTop` remains clamped — the user's view jumps upward.

**Files:** `static/js/chatHistory.js`, `static/index.html`

comments.body: Fixes applied in commit `8f50345` on `fix/dom-oom-virtualization`, cherry-picked to `develop` as `5cb59d4`. Ready for verification — all three behaviors listed above should be resolved.

All three bugs are addressed by `fix/dom-oom-virtualization` (issue #2):

- **Bug 1** (scroll-to-bottom stops at current DOM bottom): `scrollToBottom()` sets `_draining = true` and calls `_loadNewer()` in a loop until all batches are exhausted before settling at the actual last message.
- **Bug 2** (session loads at oldest message): `load()` sets `scrollTop = scrollHeight - clientHeight` after the initial render, landing at the bottom of the 50-message window.
- **Bug 3** (scroll jump during streaming prune): `_pruneTop()` inserts a height-matched spacer before removing nodes, so `scrollHeight` never dips and `scrollTop` is never clamped.

Close with the dom-oom branch filing (#2).

title: fix: scroll behavior bugs in virtualised chat history

## Summary

Two upstream commits combined to completely break the agent's ability to read local files:

1. **`3b01760` removed file tools from `ALWAYS_AVAILABLE`** — `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `grep`, `glob`, `ls` are now RAG-only. There are no keyword hints for disk file queries, so when a user says "browse /home/james/Projects/odysseus" the model never receives `read_file` in its tool list and falls back to saying "I don't have direct access to your local file system."

2. **Path confinement in `_resolve_tool_path`** — even when `read_file` is retrieved via RAG, it only allows paths under `data/` and `/tmp`. The home directory is blocked. The workspace feature that previously expanded this was removed in `e6b1009`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Odysseus
2. Ask the agent: "Can you read the files in /home/<user>/Projects/myapp?"
3. Agent responds: "I don't have direct access to your local file system"

## Expected Behaviour

Admin users should be able to ask the agent to read files in their home directory. The agent should use `read_file` and return the file contents.

## Actual Behaviour

Agent refuses, saying it cannot access the local filesystem. Two root causes:
- `read_file` is not in the tool list (no keyword hint matches)
- Even if it were, `_resolve_tool_path` would block the path

## Proposed Fix

1. Add keyword hints to `tool_index.py` that surface disk-file tools when the user mentions paths, source code, file extensions, or code-navigation verbs.
2. Expand `_tool_path_roots()` in `tool_execution.py` to include `$HOME` by default. The existing sensitive-file denylist (`.ssh`, `.gnupg`, `id_rsa`, etc.) already protects credentials. Admin gating via `tool_security.py` means non-admin users are unaffected.

## Install Method
Source

## OS
Linux
title: Filesystem access broken: read_file never surfaced + path confinement blocks home directory

## Problem

Two related bugs with the download cache indicator (the dot shown next to downloaded models):

**1. Indicator doesn't appear until page reload**

After a successful aria2c download, the download card shows "Download Complete" but the model row in the HWFit list doesn't get the cached dot (●). The dot only appears after a full page reload. The download completes correctly — the UI just doesn't reflect it.

**2. GGUF models never show the cached dot**

GGUF quantizations are often hosted in a different repo than the catalog entry (e.g., catalog shows `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct`, but the download lands under `unsloth/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct-GGUF`). The `dlDot` check only compared against `m.name`, so GGUF models never matched and never showed as cached.

**Fix:** Update `dlDot` logic and `refreshCachedModelIds` in `cookbook-hwfit.js` to also check all `m.gguf_sources[].repo` values against `_cachedModelIds`.

- `static/js/cookbookDownload.js`

The `cookbookDownload.js` fix depends on `_startManagedPolling` which is introduced by the aria2c downloader (#12). This fix ships as part of that PR.

## Problem

When adding a model to Cookbook with the llamacpp backend, users must manually supply a `ggufSource` (the HuggingFace repo ID that hosts GGUF quantizations). Most base models (e.g., `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B`) do not host their own GGUF files — community-quantized versions exist on separate repos (e.g., `bartowski/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-GGUF`). There is currently no way for the app to discover these automatically; users have to know to look for them.

## Solution

Add an auto-discovery path that searches HuggingFace for community GGUF quantizations of the base model when no static `ggufSource` is configured.

### New endpoint: `GET /api/cookbook/resolve-gguf?model_id=<repo_id>`
Calls `HfUrlResolver.find_gguf_sources(base_repo_id)` and returns a ranked list of GGUF candidates (sorted by downloads). Returns `{ sources: [...] }` or `{ error: "..." }`.

### `HfUrlResolver.find_gguf_sources(base_repo_id)`
- Extracts the model name from the repo ID (e.g., `Llama-3.1-8B` from `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B`)
- Queries `api.list_models(search=f"{model_name} GGUF", sort="downloads", limit=10, filter="gguf")`
- Returns a list of repo IDs sorted by download count

### `cookbookDownload.js` — auto-discovery on download start
When `backend === 'llamacpp'` and no `ggufSource` is present on the model object, `_runModelDownload` calls `/api/cookbook/resolve-gguf` before starting the download. If sources are found, the top result is injected as `ggufSource` and the download proceeds. If discovery fails, the download falls through to existing error handling.

## Files Changed
- `tooling/hf_url_resolver.py` — `find_gguf_sources()` method
- `routes/cookbook_routes.py` — `/api/cookbook/resolve-gguf` GET endpoint
- `static/js/cookbookDownload.js` — auto-discovery call in `_runModelDownload`

## Notes
- Discovery requires a valid HF token if the target repos are gated; public GGUF repos work without auth
- The injected `ggufSource` is not persisted back to the model config — it is resolved fresh each download
- This feature is independent of the aria2c reliability fixes in #23

## Problem

Several bugs and reliability issues in the aria2c download pipeline discovered through testing:

### Download card shows wrong filename (per-file rows)
tmux sessions are created without an explicit terminal width, defaulting to 80 columns. aria2c's `FILE:` progress lines — e.g., `FILE: ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--owner--Model/snapshots/{commit}/file.safetensors` — exceed 80 chars. tmux wraps the line; the JS progress parser's `(\S+)` regex captures only the truncated first line, which ends at the HF cache directory name rather than the actual filename. Per-file rows show the model directory as the filename instead of the real shard name.

**Fix:** Pass \`-x 220 -y 50\` to every \`tmux new-session\` call in \`cookbook_routes.py\`.

### "X of N files" stat disappears mid-download
\`aria2c_download.py\` prints \`[*] N file(s) to download\` once at startup. With \`--summary-interval=3\` and 4 parallel files (~5 lines per block), the banner scrolls out of the 200-line capture window after ~3–4 minutes. \`_parseDownloadState\` then resolves \`totalFiles\` to 0 and the file-count stat vanishes. The \`_dlFileTracker\` map correctly caches \`totalFileCount\` across ticks but the \`fileCtx\` stat read from the outer \`totalFiles\` variable instead.

**Fix:** Fall back to \`tr.totalFileCount\` when \`totalFiles\` is 0 inside the tracker block.

### HF endpoint throttling with 16 connections per file
\`conn_per_file = 16\` was causing connection throttling/rejections from the HuggingFace CDN for some models, leading to failed or stalled downloads.

**Fix:** Reduce \`conn_per_file\` from 16 to 3.

### aria2c input file uses space-indented options (non-canonical)
The aria2c input file format specifies tab-indented per-URL options. The code was using 2 spaces, which aria2c accepts but is not canonical.

**Fix:** Use tab indentation.

### \`--download-result=hide\` suppresses useful completion info
Changed to \`--download-result=full\` to expose the download result summary for debugging failures.

### No verification that files were actually downloaded
aria2c can exit 0 on partial failure in some edge cases. Added post-download check that the output directory is non-empty.

### \`hf_url_resolver.py\` fails silently when \`list_repo_files\` errors
Added HTTP API fallback when the huggingface_hub library raises an exception, and improved the \`include\` filter to also match against \`os.path.basename(f)\` so glob patterns like \`*.gguf\` work correctly for files in subdirectories.

## Files Changed
- \`tooling/aria2c_download.py\`
- \`tooling/hf_url_resolver.py\` (reliability parts only)
- \`routes/cookbook_routes.py\` (tmux width fix)
- \`static/js/cookbookRunning.js\` (totalFiles fallback)
- \`docs/project/non-obvious-behaviors.md\` (documents the tmux/scrollback/auth behaviors)

body:
## Summary

In `static/js/chat.js`, `streamingTTS` is declared with `const` inside a `try` block. Any stream error causes the `catch` block to throw a `ReferenceError` on the `streamingTTS` reference — silently swallowing the real error and leaving TTS in a broken state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a streaming chat session.
2. Trigger any stream error: disconnect mid-stream, use an endpoint that returns 503/429, or press Escape to abort.

## Expected

The catch block runs fully: TTS playback stops if active, error state is cleaned up, user sees the error.

## Actual

The catch block itself throws `ReferenceError: streamingTTS is not defined`, masking the original error. TTS may remain active. No error message is shown.

## Root Cause

```javascript
try {
    const streamingTTS = ...   // block-scoped — not visible in catch
    ...
} catch (error) {
    if (streamingTTS) { ... }  // ReferenceError: streamingTTS is not defined
}
```

## Fix

Hoist `streamingTTS` declaration before the `try` block:
```javascript
let streamingTTS = null;
try {
    streamingTTS = ...
    ...
} catch (error) {
    if (streamingTTS) { ... }
}
```

**Branch:** `fix/streamingtts-scope` — commit `9fabdc6` on `develop`. Clean branch needed for upstream PR.

## Fork status

Fixed on `develop` in commit `9fabdc6`.

## Upstream status

Not yet filed. Two-line change, no screenshot needed.

## Summary

`_append_tool_results()` in `src/agent_loop.py` injects tool execution results with `"role": "user"`, making them indistinguishable from actual user input. The model treats its own tool outputs as user-injected content and wastes multiple turns re-reading and hedging ("the user provided…") instead of acting on the results.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an agent session with any model and enable tool use.
2. Run a task that triggers 2+ tool calls across multiple rounds.
3. Observe: the model's follow-up responses reference tool results as if the user sent them.

## Root Cause

```python
# src/agent_loop.py — _append_tool_results()
messages.append(
    {"role": "user", "content": f"[Tool execution results]\n\n{tool_output_text}"}
)
```

Tool results use `"role": "user"` — identical to human input. Models trained on role-separated conversation formats interpret this as user-injected content.

## Fix

**Branch:** `fix/tool-result-role`

Two-part provider-aware fix:

**`agent_loop.py`** — use `"role": "system"` for text-based tool results (correct for OpenAI-compatible providers where system messages appear inline at their temporal position):
```python
{"role": "system", "content": f"[Tool execution results]\n\n{tool_output_text}"}
```

**`llm_core.py`** — companion fix in `_build_anthropic_payload()`: route tool-result system messages inline as user turns instead of extracting to the top-level Anthropic `system` prompt. Without this, all rounds' tool results collapse into a single out-of-order block at the top of the conversation.

```python
if m.get("role") == "system" and (m.get("content") or "").startswith("[Tool execution results]"):
    chat_messages.append({"role": "user", "content": m["content"]})
elif m.get("role") == "system":
    system_parts.append(m.get("content") or "")
```

## Upstream Status

Not reported or fixed upstream. Valid upstream contribution candidate once branch is verified.

body:
## Summary

In the native Linux Qt app (`linux_wrapper.py`), clicking external links or buttons that navigate to non-localhost URLs silently failed. The app view stayed blank or unchanged.

## Root cause

`QWebEnginePage` drops two types of navigation without overrides:

1. **Main-frame external navigation** — any link or JS that navigates the main frame to a non-localhost URL. Qt's default `acceptNavigationRequest` blocks external schemes so the app view never leaves `localhost`.
2. **`target="_blank"` and `window.open()` calls** — `createWindow()` not overridden → returns `nullptr` → request silently discarded.

## Fix applied

`linux_wrapper.py` commit `e01ded4` — `OdysseusPage(QWebEnginePage)` subclass:

```python
class OdysseusPage(QWebEnginePage):
    def acceptNavigationRequest(self, url, nav_type, is_main_frame):
        if is_main_frame and url.host() not in ('localhost', '127.0.0.1'):
            QDesktopServices.openUrl(url)
            return False
        return super().acceptNavigationRequest(url, nav_type, is_main_frame)

    def createWindow(self, win_type):
        page = QWebEnginePage(self.profile(), self)
        page.urlChanged.connect(lambda url: (QDesktopServices.openUrl(url), page.deleteLater()))
        return page
```

Both navigation paths now route to the system browser via `QDesktopServices.openUrl()`. The app view stays on `localhost`.

## Status

Fixed on `develop`. Fork-only change (Qt wrapper — not applicable upstream).

body:
## Summary

Two confirmed V8 Oilpan OOM crashes caused by unbounded DOM growth in `#chat-history`. Every message was appended as a live DOM node and never removed.

## Crash modes confirmed

**Mode 1 — Gradual accumulation during streaming:**
A 20-round agent session built up 40+ message bubbles and tool-call DOM subtrees until the V8 Oilpan C++ heap exhausted its virtual address reservation. The GC freed 419 MB → 16 MB just before the fatal allocation — confirming it's a reservation limit, not physical RAM.

**Mode 2 — Bulk session load:**
`selectSession()` rendered the entire session history in a single synchronous loop then ran `hljs.highlightElement()` on every code block. A fixed-size Oilpan pool exhausted at only 78 MB, 11 minutes after startup.

```
[pid 13269] V8 process OOM (Oilpan: Large allocation. Ran out of reservation) — 419 MB, 52 min uptime
[pid 13699] V8 process OOM (Oilpan: Large allocation. Ran out of reservation) — 78 MB, 11 min uptime
```

## Fix applied

**Crash recovery stopgap** (`linux_wrapper.py`, commit `564dd5c`): `renderProcessTerminated` signal handler auto-reloads the page via `setUrl()` on OOM/hard crash. Fork-only (Qt wrapper).

**DOM virtualization** (`static/js/chatHistory.js`, `sessions.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, commit `e01ded4`):
- `MessageWindow` class — renders only the last 50 messages on load; `IntersectionObserver` on a top sentinel loads older batches of 25 as the user scrolls up
- Scroll position preserved via `scrollHeight` delta technique
- Live pruning: caps `#chat-history` at 80 DOM children; prunes oldest 20 to a height-matched spacer, restores via `IntersectionObserver` on scroll
- Bidirectional cap at 120 nodes
- `overflow-anchor: none` on sentinels/spacers — prevents Chrome scroll-anchor from double-compensating programmatic `scrollTop`

**Upstream PR staged:** `docs/fork/upstream/drafts/06-dom-oom-virtualization.md` — awaiting screenshots before filing.

## Status

Resolved on `develop`. Upstream contribution pending screenshots.
